name: Lassonde Industries Inc.

thesis.business_description: North American manufacturer and marketer of juices, beverages, sauces, soups, and private-label food products
thesis.competitive_position: Lassonde is a niche North American beverage and food company with a strong private-label platform in Canada and the U.S., spanning juices, RTD beverages, and functional drinks. Its positioning is reinforced by broad product breadth, customization capability, multiple packaging formats, annual development of 200+ new formulas, and certifications/quality controls; the company also said its national brands outperformed the broader North American market in Q1 2026 ([Lassonde private label beverages U.S.](https://www.lassonde.com/en/private-label-beverages-us/), [Lassonde private label beverages Canada](https://www.lassonde.com/en/private-label-beverages-canada/), [Lassonde Q1 2026 results](https://www.lassonde.com/en/actualites/lassonde-industries-inc-announces-its-q1-2026-results/)).
thesis.main_shareholders: The Lassonde family controls the company through a holding vehicle (identified in ownership data as 3346625 Canada Inc.), reported to hold approximately 54-55% of shares outstanding; QV Investors Inc. holds about 5.7% and FMR LLC (Fidelity) about 5.1% ([Lassonde Industries Inc. ownership, Simply Wall St/Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/55-ownership-lassonde-industries-inc-124829972.html)).
thesis.red_flags: Q1 2026 disclosures point to softer beverage volumes from macroeconomic uncertainty and consumer-demand pressure, plus exposure to trade-policy uncertainty, including the 2026 USMCA review and tariff risk ([Lassonde Q1 2026 results](https://www.lassonde.com/en/actualites/lassonde-industries-inc-announces-its-q1-2026-results/)). The company also remains exposed to commodity, packaging, freight, and supply-chain cost inflation, and customer concentration can pressure pricing and margins ([Lassonde Q1 2026 results](https://www.lassonde.com/en/actualites/lassonde-industries-inc-announces-its-q1-2026-results/)).
thesis.insider_ownership: Insiders collectively hold approximately 55-56% of Lassonde Industries, concentrated in the Lassonde family's controlling holding vehicle; direct personal ownership by individual board members outside that vehicle is reported at under 1% ([Lassonde Industries Inc. ownership, Simply Wall St/Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/insiders-hold-56-lassonde-industries-185726836.html)).

industry: Consumer Staples / Food Products — North American manufacturer and marketer of juices, beverages, sauces, soups, and private-label food products

thesis.business_description: Canfor Corporation is a Canadian forest products company that manufactures softwood lumber across British Columbia, Alberta, the southeastern U.S., and Sweden, and also owns a majority stake in pulp and paper producer Canfor Pulp.
thesis.competitive_position: Canfor is one of the largest softwood lumber producers in North America with a geographically diversified mill footprint (BC, Alberta, US South, and Sweden via its ~77% stake in Vida AB, Sweden's largest privately-owned sawmill group), but it has been among the hardest-hit Canadian producers by U.S. softwood lumber duties — its penalty rate rose to 19.54% versus ~11% for peer West Fraser after a 2017 Commerce Department ruling — and it has been closing capacity (permanent closure of the Fox Creek, Alberta sawmill and two U.S. South mills in 2025) amid weak lumber markets and renewed October 2025 U.S. tariffs on Canadian softwood. [Canfor's Q2 loss widens amid weak market, softwood duties](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/33816342/canfor-s-q2-loss-widens-amid-weak-market-conditions-softwood-lumber-duties), [US doubling softwood duty rates against most Canadian producers](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-us-doubling-softwood-duty-rates-against-most-canadian-producers), [Fox Creek sawmill closure](https://globalnews.ca/news/12003417/fox-creek-sawmill-closure/).
thesis.main_shareholders: Ownership is concentrated with insiders/related holders reported at roughly 54.8% of shares per one Yahoo Finance snapshot, though third-party trackers disagree significantly (Simply Wall St cites ~22% insider / ~31% private company ownership) [Canfor Corp holders](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/quote/CFP.TO/holders). James A. Pattison (of the Jim Pattison Group) appears as a major director-level insider holder per an insider-trading tracker [CFP Insider Trading](https://www.insidertrades.com/canfor-co-cfpto-stock/). Figures are inconsistent across aggregators; a definitive 5%+ holder breakdown should be confirmed via Canfor's SEDAR+ management information circular.
thesis.insider_ownership: Reported insider/director ownership figures vary widely by source (from ~1% up to the mid-50% range depending on how 'insider' vs. founding-group holdings are classified), reflecting the Jim Pattison Group's historical large stake in Canfor; see [Canfor Corp holders](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/quote/CFP.TO/holders) and [CFP Insider Trading](https://www.insidertrades.com/canfor-co-cfpto-stock/). Could not verify an exact, current insider ownership percentage from an official filing in this search.
thesis.red_flags: No governance scandals or auditor concerns identified from official sources. Operationally, the company faces significant earnings pressure from escalating U.S. softwood lumber duties/tariffs and has been closing mills, which is a business risk rather than a governance red flag [Canfor's Q2 loss widens](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/33816342/canfor-s-q2-loss-widens-amid-weak-market-conditions-softwood-lumber-duties).

name: Mullen Group Ltd.

thesis.business_description: Transportation, warehousing, customs brokerage, and specialized hauling services across North America and western Canada.
thesis.competitive_position: Mullen Group says it is one of Canada’s largest logistics companies, with a portfolio of independently operated transportation and logistics businesses spanning less-than-truckload, truckload, warehousing, customs brokerage, transload and specialized hauling, plus energy- and resource-related services in western Canada ([Mullen Group homepage](https://www.mullen-group.com/), [Mullen Group news release](https://www.mullen-group.com/news/20260521-mullen-group-ltd-announces-declaration-of-monthly-dividend-140/)). Its niche is a diversified North American network with a stronger western Canada/resource-industry tilt than many general freight peers, which positions it against larger logistics and transportation operators while giving it exposure to specialized niches rather than pure commodity trucking ([Mullen Group homepage](https://www.mullen-group.com/), [Mullen Group news release](https://www.mullen-group.com/news/20260521-mullen-group-ltd-announces-declaration-of-monthly-dividend-140/)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Not disclosed in public filings
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources. I was not able to retrieve a current annual report or proxy circular from the available official sources in this session, so I could not independently verify detailed concentration or governance items beyond the company’s public website disclosures ([Mullen Group investors](https://www.mullen-group.com/investors/)).

industry: Industrials / Transportation & Logistics — Transportation, warehousing, customs brokerage, and specialized hauling services across North America and western Canada.

name: Willis Lease Finance Corporation

thesis.business_description: Aircraft engine leasing, maintenance, and related services for airlines worldwide
thesis.competitive_position: Willis Lease Finance Corporation is a niche commercial aircraft engine lessor, with its position centered on owning and leasing jet engines and related parts rather than whole aircraft, serving airlines and other operators that need flexible capacity. Its closest competitors are other engine and aircraft leasing specialists such as Engine Lease Finance and global lessors with engine portfolios, but the company’s scale and focus are much smaller and more specialized than the largest aircraft lessors.
thesis.red_flags: The main business is exposed to airline traffic cycles, engine valuation and remarketing risk, and concentration in a specialized asset class can create earnings volatility. I could not access the full annual report/proxy text through the available official pages, so no additional filing-based red flags were identified beyond the business model concentration risk.
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder/Chairman Charles F. Willis, IV is the controlling insider, holding shares via CFW Partners, L.P. (in which he holds a 1% general partner interest and 80% limited partner interest); insiders collectively hold approximately US million worth of stock (exact percentage and date not found in this search) ([Willis Lease Finance DEF 14A filings - SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001018164/000104746915004040/a2224403zdef14a.htm))

industry: Industrials / Aircraft Leasing — Aircraft engine leasing, maintenance, and related services for airlines worldwide

thesis.business_description: Great Lakes Dredge & Dock Corporation is the largest provider of dredging services in the United States, performing harbor maintenance, beach nourishment, coastal protection, and land reclamation, and has expanded into offshore wind support services.
thesis.competitive_position: GLDD operates the largest and most diverse fleet in the U.S. dredging industry (~200 specialized vessels), giving it scale advantages under the Jones Act, which restricts U.S. dredging work to domestically built/owned vessels; it has also built an Offshore Wind segment (formed 2021) as a newer growth avenue [company profile](https://jobs.theiia.org/profile/great-lakes-dredge-dock-corp/1794076/).
thesis.main_shareholders: No single controlling shareholder; ownership is spread across institutions. A February 2025 MarketBeat compilation lists Jennison Associates (~7.88%), Vanguard Group (~5.80%), AllianceBernstein (~3.95%), and TCW Group (~3.20%) as top institutional holders [MarketBeat filing](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/american-capital-advisory-llc-buys-shares-of-91578-great-lakes-dredge-dock-co-nasdaqgldd-2025-02-08). Institutional ownership estimates range from ~65% to ~78% depending on the aggregator and date [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/capital-goods/nasdaq-gldd/great-lakes-dredge-dock/ownership).
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is reported as low, roughly 3% of shares, per TipRanks-sourced data; named insiders/directors include Lasse Petterson, Ryan Levenson, Kathleen M. Shanahan, Christopher Gunsten, Eleni Beyko, Ronald Steger, and Earl L. Shipp [TipRanks ownership](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/gldd/ownership). Insider trading in late 2024/early 2025 was mixed, with buying reported exceeding selling over a 3-month window per Simply Wall St.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in this search; no governance disputes, litigation, or auditor issues surfaced.

thesis.main_shareholders: As of March 5, 2026: BlackRock, Inc. held 15.7% (2,821,467 shares), The Vanguard Group, Inc. held 12.5% (2,250,515 shares), and Mairs & Power, Inc. held 6.0% (1,071,474 shares) ([Tennant Company DEF 14A FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/97134/000110465926030889/tm261343-1_def14a.htm))
thesis.business_description: Tennant Company designs, manufactures, and markets commercial and industrial floor cleaning equipment (scrubbers, sweepers, vacuums) and related cleaning solutions sold under the Tennant and other brands.
thesis.competitive_position: Tennant is a global leader in cleaning machinery, with meaningful market share in EMEA (~10%) and APAC (~5%), competing against Alfred Kärcher, Nilfisk, Dyson, Hako and smaller regional manufacturers; it differentiates through smart/connected cleaning technology and sustainability-focused equipment. [Kalkine Media](https://kalkinemedia.com/us/news/top-stories/how-tennant-company-is-driving-operational-efficiency-across-industries)
thesis.red_flags: In early 2026, Tennant disclosed major problems with a company-wide ERP system rollout, which caused roughly $30 million in lost sales and an estimated $20+ million remediation cost; the stock dropped about 23% on the news, wiping out roughly $343 million of market cap. Multiple securities law firms (BFA Law, Hagens Berman) have since announced investigations into whether Tennant misrepresented the ERP rollout's progress to investors (e.g., claiming it was "on time and on budget" shortly before the issues emerged). [BusinessWire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260318872351/en/TNC-Investigation-Alert-BFA-Law-Investigates-Tennant-Company-After-23-Stock-Drop)

thesis.business_description: Ryerson Holding Corporation is a metals service center and value-added processor/distributor of industrial metals (stainless steel, aluminum, carbon steel, alloy steel, nickel and red metals) in coils, sheets, bars, plates, structurals and tubing, serving customers in the US, Canada, Mexico and China.
thesis.competitive_position: Ryerson is one of the largest metals service center/distribution companies in North America (founded 1842, ~4,300 employees, HQ Chicago), with scale advantages in a fragmented, commoditized metals distribution industry; it competes on breadth of inventory, processing capability and logistics rather than a structural moat, and results are cyclical with steel/aluminum pricing. See [company profile](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ryz/company/) and [Wikipedia overview](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryerson_(company)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Platinum Equity (Tom Gores) was long the controlling shareholder, holding ~55% as of Feb 2020-2022 and reducing to ~33.6% by Feb 2023 per SEC 13G/A filings; by institutional-holdings data as of Dec 31, 2025, Platinum Equity Advisors LLC held ~12.3%, with BlackRock ~10.0%, Franklin Resources ~9.0%, JB Capital Partners ~7.4%, Dimensional Fund Advisors ~6.0%, Donald Smith & Co. ~5.9%, and Vanguard ~5.4% — reflecting a multi-year secondary sell-down by Platinum Equity. Sources: [SEC DEF 14A filings](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1481582/000095017023007290/ryi-2023_proxy_statement.pdf), [Yahoo Finance holders](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/RYZ/holders/), [Fintel institutional ownership](https://fintel.io/so/us/ryi).
thesis.insider_ownership: Insiders as a group hold roughly 7% of shares per aggregator data; Chairman Michael D. Siegal individually holds about 1,825,226 shares (~3.5%) per filings; the largest individual-linked holder is Tom Gores via Platinum Equity entities (see main_shareholders, now a declining stake). Sources: [SecForm4 insider holders](https://www.secform4.com/insider-holders/1481582.html), [WallStreetZen ownership](https://www.wallstreetzen.com/stocks/us/nyse/ryz/ownership).
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; SEC 10-K filings describe only ordinary-course litigation (product liability, contract, employment matters) and an unqualified audit opinion on internal controls. Notable: former controlling shareholder Platinum Equity has been steadily selling down its stake over several years (from ~55% in 2020 to ~12% by late 2025), which is a governance/overhang item to watch but not itself a red flag. Source: [Ryerson 10-K FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1481582/000095017025024199/ryi-20241231.htm).

name: Tripadvisor, Inc.

thesis.business_description: Online travel platform providing hotel, experience, and restaurant discovery, booking, and reviews worldwide
thesis.competitive_position: Tripadvisor sits at the intersection of travel planning and bookable travel inventory: it calls itself the world’s largest online travel guidance platform and a leading global online bookable experiences platform, with TheFork as a leading European restaurant discovery and booking platform. Management says it has a durable, difficult-to-replicate asset base built on a large global audience, trusted brands, and community-driven content, while competing in experiences against OTAs and activity platforms such as Viator and in travel guidance against other travel meta and review sites.
thesis.main_shareholders: Liberty TripAdvisor Holdings, Inc. beneficially owns approximately 21.0% of issued and outstanding common stock and approximately 56.8% of total voting power (via a dual-class share structure with 10-votes-per-share Class B stock), as of October 31, 2024 ([Tripadvisor DEF 14A / Liberty TripAdvisor filings](https://ir.tripadvisor.com/static-files/b5c83b2c-e8dd-401d-bfad-b18f69af1097))
thesis.red_flags: Tripadvisor disclosed $3.3 million of shareholder-activism-related costs in Q1 2026, indicating ongoing activist pressure. The company also flags dependence on discretionary travel demand and competitive, fast-changing digital travel markets, and its Hotels & Other segment was down 11% year over year in LTM 1Q26, showing legacy business pressure.
thesis.insider_ownership: Liberty TripAdvisor Holdings, Inc. is the controlling insider, holding approximately 56.8% of total voting power as of October 31, 2024 ([Tripadvisor DEF 14A / Liberty TripAdvisor filings](https://ir.tripadvisor.com/static-files/b5c83b2c-e8dd-401d-bfad-b18f69af1097))

industry: Consumer Discretionary / Travel Services — Online travel platform providing hotel, experience, and restaurant discovery, booking, and reviews worldwide

name: G-III Apparel Group, Ltd.

thesis.business_description: Designs, sources, and markets licensed and owned apparel, accessories, and retail brands
thesis.competitive_position: G-III is a branded apparel and accessories platform with a portfolio of 30+ owned and licensed brands, including DKNY, Karl Lagerfeld, Donna Karan, Vilebrequin, and Calvin Klein, which it markets through design, sourcing, distribution, and licensing. Its niche is built on managing globally recognized fashion brands rather than competing as a pure manufacturing house, putting it alongside other brand-licensing apparel groups and fashion marketers such as PVH and Tapestry in adjacent categories. [G-III Apparel Group](https://www.giii.com)
thesis.red_flags: The company’s business is exposed to brand-license dependence, fashion-cycle volatility, sourcing and inventory execution, and tariff/supply-chain risk, which can pressure margins and demand. No specific governance or accounting issue was identified from the official sources reviewed. [G-III Apparel Group ARS filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/821002/000110465926055627/0001104659-26-055627-index.htm), [G-III Apparel Group investor relations](https://ir.giii.com/financials/sec-filings?items_per_page=10&items_per_page_toggle=0&mobile=1&field_nir_sec_cik_target_id=&field_nir_sec_date_filed_value=&order=field_nir_sec_form&sort=desc&page=144)
thesis.insider_ownership: Chairman/CEO Morris Goldfarb beneficially owned approximately 10.3% of common stock (4,703,922 shares) as of April 17, 2023, up from 7.8% (4,092,461 shares) in June 2022; insiders collectively own approximately 14% of the company (worth about US3 million at the time reported) ([G-III Apparel Group DEF 14A FY2023](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/821002/000155837023008325/giii-20230608xdef14a.htm))

industry: Consumer Discretionary / Apparel — Designs, sources, and markets licensed and owned apparel, accessories, and retail brands

name: Trican Well Service Ltd.

thesis.business_description: Oilfield services provider supplying fracturing, cementing, coiled tubing, nitrogen, and chemical solutions in Western Canada
thesis.competitive_position: Trican describes itself as the largest pressure pumping service company in Canada and says it is focused on fracturing, cementing, coiled tubing, nitrogen services and chemical sales across the Western Canadian Sedimentary Basin ([Trican press release](https://tricanwellservice.com/trican-reports-first-quarter-results-for-2026-and-declares-quarterly-dividend/), [Trican investor relations](https://tricanwellservice.com/investors/)). Its positioning is driven by fleet modernization (Tier 4 DGB, electric ancillary equipment and a planned natural-gas-fueled fracturing fleet) and the Iron Horse acquisition, which expanded coiled-tubing-integrated fracturing capabilities against competitors in Canadian pressure pumping such as Secure Energy and STEP Energy Services ([Trican press release](https://tricanwellservice.com/trican-reports-first-quarter-results-for-2026-and-declares-quarterly-dividend/)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Not disclosed in public filings
thesis.red_flags: Trican flags meaningful exposure to commodity-price volatility and “significant pricing pressure” in completion services, reflecting a competitive market and balanced supply-demand in pressure pumping ([Trican press release](https://tricanwellservice.com/trican-reports-first-quarter-results-for-2026-and-declares-quarterly-dividend/)). The company also carries execution risk from its capital-intensive fleet modernization and ERP rollout, while the latest annual meeting results showed one director nominee with relatively high withheld votes (10.58%), though no formal governance issue was disclosed ([Trican annual meeting results](https://tricanwellservice.com/app/uploads/2026/05/Press-Release-2026-Annual-Meeting-Results.pdf)).

industry: Energy / Oil & Gas Services — Oilfield services provider supplying fracturing, cementing, coiled tubing, nitrogen, and chemical solutions in Western Canada

name: Stepan Company

thesis.business_description: Manufactures surfactants, polyurethane polyols, and specialty chemicals for consumer, industrial, and agricultural markets
thesis.competitive_position: Stepan is a niche global specialty and intermediate chemicals supplier in surfactants, polymer/polyol, and specialty products, serving home and industrial cleaning, crop protection, construction, and other end markets. Its public filings show it competes with large chemical players such as BASF, Dow, Nouryon, and other regional formulators, while its scale and product mix are narrower than the biggest diversified chemical companies.
thesis.main_shareholders: F. Quinn Stepan and Stepan family interests were historically the largest beneficial holders (24.1% as of Feb 2004 per DEF 14A); no confirmed current-year percentage was located in this search ([Stepan DEF 14A 2004](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/94049/000119312504053316/ddef14a.htm))
thesis.red_flags: Stepan’s filings highlight exposure to cyclical raw-material and energy costs, end-market demand swings, and customer concentration in its formulations businesses. The company also faces ordinary chemical-industry regulatory/environmental compliance risk, and its filings show some ownership concentration among a few large institutional holders.

industry: Materials / Specialty Chemicals — Manufactures surfactants, polyurethane polyols, and specialty chemicals for consumer, industrial, and agricultural markets

name: XPEL, Inc.

thesis.business_description: Automotive and architectural paint protection film, window film, and coatings for vehicle and building surfaces
thesis.competitive_position: XPEL is a niche specialty automotive protection company focused on paint protection film, window film, and related protection products sold through installers and dealers. Its position appears strongest in premium aftermarket protection, with competition coming from major film and coatings brands such as 3M, LLumar, and SunTek, and its investor materials emphasize a global installer/distributor network as a key channel advantage ([XPEL SEC filings](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1767258/000176725826000032/0001767258-26-000032-index.htm), [XPEL SEC filings page](https://investor.xpel.com/financials/sec-filings/default.aspx)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Institutional investors hold approximately 68.0% of shares in aggregate as a group, with individual/public holders making up the remainder ([XPEL ownership - GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/XPEL/ownership))
thesis.red_flags: XPEL’s proxy disclosure highlights that the company has no policy restricting employees or directors from hedging their equity exposure, which is a governance watchpoint ([XPEL 2026 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1767258/000176725826000043/0001767258-26-000043-index.htm)). Based on the official materials reviewed, no major regulatory or accounting issues were identified; however, the company remains exposed to competitive pressure in its niche film and coatings market and to concentration in its installed-base/channel model ([XPEL SEC filings page](https://investor.xpel.com/financials/sec-filings/default.aspx), [XPEL SEC filing index](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1767258/000176725826000032/0001767258-26-000032-index.htm)).
thesis.insider_ownership: Company insiders (officers and directors) hold approximately 9.3% of shares as a group ([XPEL ownership - GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/XPEL/ownership))

industry: Materials / Specialty Chemicals — Automotive and architectural paint protection film, window film, and coatings for vehicle and building surfaces

name: Canada Goose Holdings Inc.

thesis.business_description: Premium outerwear, apparel, footwear, and accessories for global cold-weather and lifestyle markets
thesis.competitive_position: Canada Goose is a global performance-luxury outerwear brand with a strong niche in premium cold-weather apparel, leveraging Canadian heritage, technical craftsmanship, and year-round expansion into apparel, footwear, and accessories. Management says revenue growth was supported by stronger DTC conversion, improved wholesale performance, and momentum across an expanded product offering, positioning it against premium outerwear competitors such as Moncler and The North Face in the high-end functional apparel market ([Canada Goose Investor Relations](https://investor.canadagoose.com/), [Canada Goose FY2026 Results](https://investor.canadagoose.com/news/news-details/2026/Canada-Goose-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-Fiscal-2026-Results/default.aspx)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Bain Capital owned approximately 60.5% of outstanding multiple voting shares (about 55.5% of combined voting power), and CEO Dani Reiss owned approximately 39.5% of multiple voting shares (about 36.2% of total voting power), as of March 30 (year per source). Other large institutional holders of subordinate voting shares include Morgan Stanley (13.59%), Fidelity Management (11.50%) and Manulife Financial (8.49%) ([Canada Goose Holdings ownership, Value Chain Analysis](https://valuechainanalysis.com/blogs/company-ecosystem-ownership/canadagoose)). Note: Bain Capital and Dani Reiss have subsequently sold down portions of their multiple voting share stakes, so current percentages may be lower ([Bain Capital, Dani Reiss to sell 9.9M Canada Goose shares, Private Capital Journal](https://privatecapitaljournal.com/bain-capital-dani-reiss-sell-9-9m-canada-goose-shares/)).
thesis.red_flags: The company disclosed an $8.4 million store impairment tied to underperforming locations, and its outlook highlights softer consumer demand, travel weakness, raw-material inflation, supply-chain cost pressure, and unchanged tariff assumptions. It also notes broad forward-looking uncertainty in a highly competitive and rapidly changing environment ([Canada Goose FY2026 Results](https://investor.canadagoose.com/news/news-details/2026/Canada-Goose-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-Fiscal-2026-Results/default.aspx)).
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder/CEO Dani Reiss and aligned insiders hold multiple voting shares giving them strategic control; Reiss individually held approximately 39.5% of multiple voting shares (about 36.2% of total voting power) as of the source date, though this has since been reduced by share sales ([Canada Goose Holdings ownership, Value Chain Analysis](https://valuechainanalysis.com/blogs/company-ecosystem-ownership/canadagoose)).

industry: Consumer Discretionary / Apparel — Premium outerwear, apparel, footwear, and accessories for global cold-weather and lifestyle markets

name: Upbound Group, Inc.

thesis.business_description: Lease-to-own and financial health services for consumers and retailers in the U.S.
thesis.competitive_position: Upbound Group operates a niche U.S. lease-to-own model under brands such as Rent-A-Center and Acima, serving customers who want flexible payment options for furniture, electronics, appliances, and other durable goods. Its position comes from a scaled store and digital footprint in this installment/lease-to-own segment, where it competes with Aaron’s and smaller local lease-to-own operators. [SEC filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/933036/000110465925015439/0001104659-25-015439-index.html)
thesis.red_flags: The main risk is exposure to the lease-to-own customer base, which is typically more credit-sensitive and cyclical, so performance can weaken if consumer stress rises. I was not able to verify a current beneficial-ownership table from the filing directory, so ownership concentration and insider control should be confirmed against the latest proxy or 10-K. [SEC filing directory](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/933036/000110465925015439/)
thesis.insider_ownership: CEO Mitchell Fadel held approximately 1.7% of common stock (910,015 shares) as of April 9, 2024; director Jeffrey Brown held less than 1% (188,794 shares); insiders collectively hold approximately 1.37% of the company ([Upbound Group DEF 14A FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/933036/000110465924050354/tm242920d5_def14a.htm))

industry: Consumer Discretionary / Specialty Retail — Lease-to-own and financial health services for consumers and retailers in the U.S.

name: CRA International, Inc.

thesis.business_description: Global consulting firm providing economic, financial, and strategic advisory services
thesis.competitive_position: CRA International is a niche, senior-led consulting firm focused on economic litigation, management consulting, and expert advisory work for law firms, corporations, accounting firms, and governments. Its website describes it as a leading global consulting firm with analytics-driven, fact-based expertise, competing in specialized advisory and litigation-economics work rather than broad generalist consulting ([CRA About](https://www.crai.com/about/)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Per the FY2012 proxy (dated data), Royce & Associates, LLC held 15.3%, Wasatch Advisors, Inc. held 13.3%, Artisan Partners held 9.0%, BlackRock, Inc. held 6.2%, and FMR LLC held 5.8%; more recent 5% holder figures were not found in this search ([CRA International DEF 14A FY2012](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001053706/000104746912004881/a2208837zf1_def-14a.pdf))

The most recent SEC filing used here is a Form 8-K, not a proxy statement, and it did not disclose ownership concerns or material governance issues; no 5% beneficial owners were found in the filing text reviewed ([SEC 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1053706/000105370626000013/crai-20260507.htm)).

industry: Business Services / Consulting — Global consulting firm providing economic, financial, and strategic advisory services

name: American Public Education, Inc.

thesis.business_description: Online and campus-based postsecondary education for military, healthcare, and working-adult students across the U.S.
thesis.competitive_position: American Public Education is a niche postsecondary education provider focused on career-oriented programs through American Public University System, Rasmussen University, and Hondros College of Nursing, which positions it in military/public-service and healthcare-oriented education rather than broad four-year higher education. Its website describes it as a provider of career-focused, affordable programs, and its SEC filings classify it as educational services rather than a general university system. [American Public Education](https://www.apei.com/) [SEC filing index](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1201792/000120179226000008/0001201792-26-000008-index.htm)
thesis.main_shareholders: Not disclosed in public filings
thesis.red_flags: The company operates in a heavily regulated education industry and depends on enrollment, retention, and program outcomes across its schools, so adverse regulatory changes or enrollment softness could pressure results. Official filings available here do not show a material ownership disclosure table, and the accessible SEC pages provided do not identify specific governance or accounting issues. [SEC filing index](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1201792/000120179226000008/0001201792-26-000008-index.htm) [American Public Education](https://www.apei.com/)

industry: Consumer Discretionary / Education Services — Online and campus-based postsecondary education for military, healthcare, and working-adult students across the U.S.

name: Sinclair, Inc.

thesis.business_description: Television broadcasting and local news production across U.S. markets with digital media and sports content
thesis.competitive_position: Sinclair is a diversified media company with national reach, anchored by 177 broadcast television stations in 79 markets and a strong local-news and sports footprint, plus Tennis Channel and multicast networks such as CHARGE!, Comet, ROAR and The Nest ([Sinclair website](https://sbgi.net/), [Sinclair 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1971213/000197121326000025/sbgi-20260331.htm)). Its niche is the combination of local broadcast scale and distribution-driven revenue streams such as retransmission consent, advertising, and owned networks, competing with other local station groups and digital-first video platforms ([Sinclair 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1971213/000197121326000025/sbgi-20260331.htm)).
thesis.main_shareholders: David Smith, Frederick Smith, J. Duncan Smith, and Robert Smith collectively hold substantially all of Sinclair’s Class B Common Stock and some Class A Common Stock; the filing does not provide a public percentage ownership table for them ([Sinclair 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1971213/000197121326000025/sbgi-20260331.htm)).
thesis.red_flags: The company faces meaningful regulatory risk around FCC ownership rules, retransmission-consent negotiations, NextGen TV/ATSC 1.0 transition, and changes to indecency, political-ad rules, and station-ownership limits ([Sinclair 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1971213/000197121326000025/sbgi-20260331.htm)). It also highlights industry pressure from cord-cutting, subscriber churn, weaker live TV viewing, and reliance on advertising and network/programming relationships ([Sinclair 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1971213/000197121326000025/sbgi-20260331.htm)).

industry: Communication Services / Broadcasting — Television broadcasting and local news production across U.S. markets with digital media and sports content

thesis.business_description: National Presto Industries is a diversified manufacturer operating in three segments: small kitchen appliances (under the Presto brand), diapers/adult incontinence products, and defense products (ammunition and munitions components for the U.S. military).
thesis.competitive_position: National Presto's housewares segment is a long-established but secondary player behind larger kitchen-appliance brands, while its defense segment has become an increasingly important earnings driver through U.S. government ammunition contracts; the company is distinctive for a conservative, debt-averse balance sheet with a large cash/government-bond position, as highlighted in a 2009 Forbes profile [Forbes profile via Shareholder Forum](https://shareholderforum.com/NYSSA/Reports/20091116_Forbes.htm).
thesis.main_shareholders: Company is closely controlled by the Cohen family through a voting trust. A 2014 SEC proxy (DEF 14A) discloses that fourteen trusts related to the Cohen family and extended family entered a voting trust agreement covering 1,669,664 common shares, trusteed by then-CEO Maryjo Cohen, set to terminate November 3, 2027 absent unanimous extension [National Presto DEF 14A FY2014](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080172/000089710114000471/def141154_def14a.htm). A third-party tracker (unverified against a current filing) estimates Maryjo R. Cohen individually holds ~23.84% of shares.
thesis.insider_ownership: Officers and directors as a group held approximately 30.0% of shares per the 2014 proxy (30.1% in the 2011 proxy) [National Presto DEF 14A FY2014](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080172/000089710114000471/def141154_def14a.htm); [National Presto DEF 14A FY2011](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080172/000089710111000597/presto111691_def14a.htm). Maryjo Cohen has served as CEO since 1976 and chairs the voting trust; the Phillips Foundation (tied to the family's origin through Lewis E. Phillips) also holds shares per the 2018 proxy [National Presto DEF 14A FY2018](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080172/000089710118000361/presto180737_def14a.htm).
thesis.red_flags: The company has long been characterized by media as family-dominated/insular governance (Cohen family voting trust controlling the board for decades), which some observers view as a related-party/entrenchment concern rather than a disclosed violation; no litigation, auditor, or dilution red flags were identified from official sources [Forbes profile via Shareholder Forum](https://shareholderforum.com/NYSSA/Reports/20091116_Forbes.htm).

thesis.business_description: Major Drilling Group International is a Canadian provider of specialized contract drilling services to the mining industry, including exploration, delineation, underground, and other drilling services worldwide.
thesis.competitive_position: Major Drilling is one of the largest mineral/mining drilling contractors globally, with a broad international fleet and footprint, but operates in a cyclical, commoditized services industry tied to mining capex cycles; ownership data (below) shows no single dominant shareholder supports a widely-held, institutionally-monitored governance structure [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsx-mdi/major-drilling-group-international-shares/ownership).
thesis.main_shareholders: No controlling shareholder. FMR LLC (Fidelity) is the largest holder at approximately 8.67% (~7.1 million shares), followed by Royce & Associates (~5.87%), Beutel Goodman & Company (~4.62%), Dimensional Fund Advisors (~2.79%), Industrielle Alliance (~2.66%), and Sprott (~2.17%); the top 25 shareholders combined own 38.73% [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsx-mdi/major-drilling-group-international-shares/ownership).
thesis.insider_ownership: Individual insider ownership is small, roughly 0.3% of shares (~250,000 shares) per Simply Wall St, though GuruFocus notes its data (drawn only from direct Form 3/4/5 filings) may understate true indirect insider holdings [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsx-mdi/major-drilling-group-international-shares/ownership); [GuruFocus ownership](https://sgp.gurufocus.com/stock/TSX:MDI/ownership). Insider selling (Jo Zurel, John Davies, Ben Graham) exceeded insider buying (Kimberly Keating, Denis Larocque, Ghislain LeBlanc) in late 2025 in dollar terms.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; shares are widely held with no dilution or governance controversy surfaced in this search.

thesis.business_description: Marcus & Millichap is a national commercial real estate services firm providing investment sales brokerage, financing, research, and advisory services, with particular strength in the $1 million-to-$10 million private-client property segment.
thesis.competitive_position: Marcus & Millichap describes itself as the leading national investment brokerage firm in the private-client ($1M-$10M) commercial real estate segment, built on a large network of agents; it was spun out of parent Marcus & Millichap Company (MMC) and IPO'd in November 2013, with MMC distributing 80% of shares to its own shareholders at that time [Marcus & Millichap 10-K FY2019](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1578732/000119312520058202/d825656d10k.htm).
thesis.main_shareholders: Institutional ownership is estimated at roughly 62.9% of shares, with insiders at roughly 37.1%, and the top 25 shareholders combined holding 91.85% per Simply Wall St [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/real-estate-management-and-development/nyse-mmi/marcus-millichap/ownership). Top institutional holders per a MarketBeat compilation include Vanguard Group (~9.73%), Reinhart Partners (~5.52%), Royce & Associates (~4.48%), and Lord Abbett (~2.02%).
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder and Chairman George M. Marcus (co-founded the firm in 1971 in Palo Alto with William A. Millichap) is the most notable insider holder; Simply Wall St identifies him as having made the largest individual insider sale in the trailing 12 months (~$3.0 million at $34.24/share) [Simply Wall St insider sales news](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/real-estate/nyse-mmi/marcus-millichap/news/have-insiders-sold-marcus-millichap-inc-nysemmi-shares-recen). Overall insider ownership is estimated around 37.1% combined; GuruFocus reports net insider selling and no insider purchases over the trailing 18 months, with other named insiders including CEO Hessam Nadji, Norma J. Lawrence, John David Parker, and Don C. Watters.
thesis.red_flags: Sustained net insider selling over 18 months (per GuruFocus), including a large sale by founder/Chairman George Marcus, is worth monitoring but is disclosed, routine insider activity rather than a governance violation; no litigation, auditor, or dilution issues were identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Daktronics designs, manufactures, and services large-scale electronic display systems — including scoreboards, video boards, digital billboards, and transportation message signs — for sports venues, commercial, and public-sector customers worldwide.
thesis.competitive_position: Daktronics is a longstanding global leader in LED display/scoreboard technology, founded in 1968 by two South Dakota State University engineering professors, operating across Commercial, Live Events, High School Park & Recreation, Transportation, and International segments, giving it diversified end-market exposure within a niche hardware/display category [Daktronics about us](https://www.daktronics.com/company).
thesis.main_shareholders: Alta Fox Capital Management is the largest outside shareholder, reported at roughly 11.97% in a 2025 MarketBeat compilation that also lists Duquesne Family Office and Vanguard among top holders [MarketBeat: Alta Fox Capital position increase](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/daktronics-inc-nasdaqdakt-position-increased-by-alta-fox-capital-management-llc-2025-05-03). Alta Fox has sold significant blocks of stock during 2025 (e.g., a reported ~$13.7 million sale on 10 Dec 2025 and ~$14.9 million sale on 29 May 2025 per Simply Wall St's insider-sale tracking, treating Alta Fox as a 10%+ holder).
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership (officers/directors, including activist holder Alta Fox in some classifications) is reported at roughly 4.6%-7.9% depending on source and date [MarketBeat filing, Aug 2026](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/filing-daktronics-inc-dakt-shares-bought-by-lazard-asset-management-llc-2026-08-03/). Named management/insiders include Reece A. Kurtenbach, Bradley T. Wiemann, John Patrick Friel, Andrew David Siegel, and Matthew John Kurtenbach; sources disagree on the current CEO (one profile lists Ramesh Jayaraman, an earlier record lists Bradley T. Wiemann as President/CEO), suggesting a recent leadership change that should be confirmed against the company's latest filings.
thesis.red_flags: Large, repeated share sales by top shareholder Alta Fox Capital Management in 2025 are worth monitoring (disclosed, not necessarily adverse), and there is some ambiguity/inconsistency across sources about current CEO identity that should be confirmed; no litigation or auditor concerns were identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Seneca Foods Corporation is a leading North American processor and packer of canned and frozen vegetables and fruit, selling under its own brands and private label to retail, food service, and industrial customers.
thesis.competitive_position: Seneca is one of the largest vegetable canners in North America with a vertically integrated network of processing plants, benefiting from scale in a mature, low-growth commodity-food category; it maintains a dual-class share structure (Class A/Class B) typical of legacy family-influenced food companies [Seneca Foods ownership discussion](https://www.itiger.com/news/2516303405).
thesis.main_shareholders: The Seneca Foods Pension Plan is reported as the largest shareholder at roughly 15% of shares outstanding, followed by Dimensional Fund Advisors LP (~7.3%) and Chairman Kraig Kayser (~6.5%) per a Simply Wall St ownership analysis [Seneca Foods institutional investor article](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/food-beverage-tobacco/nasdaq-sene.a/seneca-foods/news/seneca-foods-corporations-nasdaqsenea-institutional-investor/amp). Institutional ownership estimates range from 41% to 48% depending on source and date.
thesis.insider_ownership: Chairman Kraig Kayser holds approximately 6.5% of shares and is cited as the third-largest shareholder; CEO Paul Palmby directly holds about 2.7% [Seneca Foods institutional investor article](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/food-beverage-tobacco/nasdaq-sene.a/seneca-foods/news/seneca-foods-corporations-nasdaqsenea-institutional-investor/amp). Overall insider ownership estimates range from ~8.4% (MarketBeat) to ~16% (Simply Wall St), with the discrepancy likely tied to differing definitions and the company's dual Class A/Class B share structure.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in this search; note the company's dual-class (Class A/Class B) share structure, a standard feature that concentrates voting influence but was not linked to any specific dispute or dilution event found here.

thesis.main_shareholders: Per the March 2024 proxy: BlackRock, Inc. held 14.3% (3,377,590 shares), The Vanguard Group held 9.3% (2,200,611 shares), FMR LLC held 7.6% (1,800,907 shares), Dimensional Fund Advisors LP held 6.1% (1,443,055 shares), and Wasatch Advisors LP held 5.6% (1,328,778 shares) ([LGI Homes DEF 14A FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1580670/000158067024000020/lgih-20240315.htm))
thesis.insider_ownership: Chairman/CEO Eric Lipar held approximately 9.8% of shares (2,319,728 shares); all executive officers and directors as a group (10 persons) held 2,882,815 shares, roughly 12% of shares outstanding ([LGI Homes DEF 14A FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1580670/000158067024000020/lgih-20240315.htm))
thesis.business_description: LGI Homes is a residential homebuilder that acquires and develops land and constructs spec-built, entry-level single-family homes aimed primarily at first-time homebuyers and renters converting to ownership.
thesis.competitive_position: LGI Homes is a top-10 U.S. public homebuilder by closings (~10,000 homes/year across 21 states), having scaled from a Texas startup into one of the largest entry-level-focused builders through a systemized, volume-driven build-and-sell model; it owns roughly 87% of its lot inventory, capturing developer profit in-house rather than relying on third-party land developers. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/articles/lgi-homes-stock-climbs-56-134600727.html)
thesis.red_flags: LGI Homes and joint-venture partner loanDepot face a class-action lawsuit (Florida) alleging a deceptive "improper home-sales scheme" that uses misleading low advertised payments and high-pressure, scripted sales tactics to push renters into mortgages via LGI Mortgage Solutions LLC, potentially acting as an unlicensed loan originator. Separately, a certified class action by a former sales rep (filed 2023, class certified Dec. 2024) alleges Colorado wage-and-hour violations (unpaid overtime, missed rest breaks, improper wage deductions). [HousingWire](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/lgi-loandepot-class-action/)

name: Middlesex Water Company

thesis.business_description: Regulated water and wastewater utility services in New Jersey and Delaware
thesis.competitive_position: Middlesex Water is a regulated water and wastewater utility with a concentrated franchise in New Jersey and Delaware, giving it a defensible local service-territory niche rather than a broad competitive landscape. Its position is anchored by exclusive or regulated service areas and long-lived utility infrastructure rather than direct product competition ([Middlesex Water Company](https://www.middlesexwater.com), [Middlesex Water IR SEC filings](https://investors.middlesexwater.com/financial-information/sec-filings)).
thesis.main_shareholders: BlackRock, Inc. is currently the largest shareholder with approximately 15% of shares outstanding; State Street Global Advisors, Inc. holds approximately 10%, and The Vanguard Group, Inc. holds approximately 7.7% ([Middlesex Water ownership tracker](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/72-ownership-shares-middlesex-water-123201806.html))
thesis.red_flags: The company’s risk profile is typical of a regulated utility: geographic concentration in New Jersey and Delaware, regulatory dependence on state utility commissions, and exposure to environmental compliance and infrastructure spending needs ([Middlesex Water Company](https://www.middlesexwater.com)). None identified from official sources beyond those ordinary utility risks ([Middlesex Water IR SEC filings](https://investors.middlesexwater.com/financial-information/sec-filings)).
thesis.insider_ownership: All 18 elected directors and executive officers as a group held 232,535 shares, approximately 1.32% of shares outstanding, as of March 25, 2025; CEO Dennis Doll individually held approximately 0.5% ([Middlesex Water DEF 14A FY2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/66004/000117494725000561/msex-20241231.htm))

industry: Utilities / Water — Regulated water and wastewater utility services in New Jersey and Delaware

name: Winnebago Industries, Inc.

thesis.business_description: Manufactures RVs, campers, and marine boats for North American outdoor recreation markets
thesis.competitive_position: Winnebago Industries is a North American premium outdoor recreation manufacturer whose portfolio spans Winnebago-branded motorhomes and towables plus premium marine brands, giving it a differentiated position versus RV peers like Thor Industries and REV Group and adjacent marine competitors. The company says it is a leading North American manufacturer of premium outdoor recreation products, and its brand portfolio and focus on the premium end support its niche position ([Winnebago Industries](https://www.winnebagoind.com/)).
thesis.main_shareholders: BlackRock, Inc. held 14.60% of common stock (4,929,621 shares) and Dimensional Fund Advisors LP held 6.36% (2,146,157 shares) as of Oct 20, 2020 ([Winnebago DEF 14A FY2020](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/107687/000114036120024343/nc10014631x4_def14a.htm))
thesis.red_flags: Winnebago’s filings show meaningful cyclicality and exposure to discretionary consumer demand in RVs and marine products, plus execution risk from product/segment mix shifts and dealer inventory changes. I could not reliably retrieve the company’s latest proxy or 10-K accession through the available SEC search tools, so this answer uses the company website for business description and notes that shareholder percentages are not fully verified from primary filings.
thesis.insider_ownership: Insiders (directors and executive officers) own approximately 3.9% of shares ([Simply Wall St - Winnebago ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/automobiles/nyse-wgo/winnebago-industries/ownership))

industry: Consumer Discretionary / Recreational Vehicles — Manufactures RVs, campers, and marine boats for North American outdoor recreation markets

thesis.insider_ownership: Founder/Chairman Randolph L. Marten is the controlling insider: as of Feb 29, 2008, he held 23.6% of shares (5,126,257 shares) and all directors/executive officers as a group held 30.9% (6,831,187 shares); by Feb 17, 2020 his direct holdings had grown to 11,685,828 shares plus options (percentage not restated in the source found, share count growth partly reflects a stock split) ([Marten Transport DEF 14A FY2008/FY2020](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/799167/000143774920005228/mrtn20200311_def14a.htm))
thesis.business_description: Marten Transport is a truckload carrier specializing in temperature-controlled and insulated transportation of food, beverages, and other consumer packaged goods across the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, along with dedicated and brokerage logistics services.
thesis.competitive_position: Marten is one of the largest and best-capitalized carriers focused specifically on the temperature-sensitive truckload segment, competing against C.R. England, Prime Inc., Stevens Transport, U.S. Xpress and others in a highly fragmented market; its scale and capitalization position it as a leader within this specialized niche rather than the broader, more commoditized dry-van trucking market. [Umbrex](https://umbrex.com/resources/company-profiles/marten-transport/)
thesis.red_flags: Marten disclosed a 2021 data-breach/cyberattack affecting ~35,294 current and former employees' and applicants' data, settled via a $520,000 class-action settlement. The company has also faced recurring driver wage-and-hour lawsuits (e.g., California claims over unpaid layover/sleeper-berth time and missed breaks). No SEC investigation or accounting red flags were found. [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/litigation/class-supports-marten-transports-520k-data-breach-settlement)

name: The Monarch Cement Company

thesis.business_description: Cement manufacturing for Midwest customers
thesis.competitive_position: The Monarch Cement Company is a long-established regional cement producer, and its website emphasizes quality and efficient, technology-enabled manufacturing rather than scale expansion ([Monarch Cement Company](https://monarchcement.com/)). I could not verify a current SEC filing that discloses market share or a peer-comparison section for Monarch Cement itself, so the best official characterization available from public sources is that it operates as a niche regional supplier with a narrow product focus ([Monarch Cement Company](https://monarchcement.com/)).
thesis.main_shareholders: As of Feb 14, 2014 (dated data): Byron K. Radcliff held a combined 10.40% of Capital Stock and Class B Capital Stock, Walter H. Wulf, Jr. held a combined 8.92%, and Franklin Resources Inc. held a combined 3.55% (5.40% of Capital Stock alone) ([Monarch Cement Co DEF 14A FY2014](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000067517/000006751714000004/mcem-def14aproxy2014.htm))
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources. I was not able to locate a current SEC annual report or proxy statement for Monarch Cement in the public EDGAR results available through this research pass, so ownership concentration, related-party issues, and other risks were not publicly verifiable from those filings ([SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/)).
thesis.insider_ownership: All directors and executive officers as a group (15 persons) held a combined 25.25% of Capital Stock and Class B Capital Stock per the FY2012 proxy (dated data; more recent figures not found in this search) ([Monarch Cement Co DEF 14A FY2012](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000067517/000006751713000008/fullproxy2013.htm))

industry: Materials / Construction Materials — Cement manufacturing for Midwest customers

name: Douglas Dynamics, Inc.

thesis.business_description: Manufacturer and upfitter of work truck attachments and snow and ice control equipment in North America
thesis.competitive_position: Douglas Dynamics says it is North America’s premier manufacturer and upfitter of commercial work truck attachments and equipment, with brands trusted across the snow and ice control and truck upfitting industries for more than 75 years ([Douglas Dynamics IR](https://ir.douglasdynamics.com)). Its niche is built around work-truck attachments rather than broad equipment manufacturing, which positions it against specialized competitors in snow and ice control and upfitting markets rather than general industrial OEMs ([Douglas Dynamics IR](https://ir.douglasdynamics.com)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Not disclosed in public filings
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.

industry: Industrials / Specialty Equipment — Manufacturer and upfitter of work truck attachments and snow and ice control equipment in North America

thesis.business_description: Unitil Corporation is a holding company for regulated electric and natural gas distribution utilities in New Hampshire, Massachusetts, and Maine (Unitil Energy, Fitchburg Gas and Electric, Northern Utilities) plus Granite State, an interstate natural gas pipeline.
thesis.competitive_position: Unitil operates small, geographically clustered regulated New England utility franchises (approximately 108,500 electric and 88,400 natural gas customers per its FY2023 10-K), giving it a stable, rate-regulated monopoly-style moat typical of small-cap regulated utilities, though its small scale limits growth relative to larger regional peers [Unitil 10-K FY2023](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/755001/000095017024014186/utl-20231231.htm).
thesis.main_shareholders: No controlling shareholder; large institutional index holders dominate. A Simply Wall St profile cites BlackRock (~18.2%), Vanguard Group (~8.6%), State Street Global Advisors (~4.0%), and Wellington Management (~3.3%) as top holders [Unitil ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/utilities/nyse-utl/unitil/ownership), while MarketBeat separately estimates institutional ownership at ~76.76%.
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is low, around 2.0%-2.2% of shares per Simply Wall St (~2.2%) and MarketBeat (~2.03%) [Unitil ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/utilities/nyse-utl/unitil/ownership). No single named insider holder with a meaningfully large stake was identified in this search.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; as a rate-regulated utility, Unitil is subject to standard regulatory oversight but no governance disputes, litigation, or auditor issues surfaced.

thesis.business_description: AGT Food and Ingredients was a globally diversified food company processing and distributing pulses, rice, milled wheat, pasta, spices, and other packaged foods, reaching consumers in over 100 countries through a global manufacturing network, headquartered in Regina, Saskatchewan and founded by Murad Al-Katib and Hüseyin Arslan.
thesis.competitive_position: IMPORTANT DATA-QUALITY FLAG: AGT Food and Ingredients was taken private and delisted from the Toronto Stock Exchange on April 17, 2019, following a C$18.00/share buyout by a group led by CEO Murad Al-Katib with financing from Fairfax Financial Holdings and Point North Capital; shareholders approved the deal on February 5, 2019 (72.5% of votes cast) and the Ontario Superior Court approved it on February 11, 2019 [AGT Food and Ingredients completes plan of arrangement](https://www.torys.com/en/work/2018/12/7d30a3c1-c0eb-48be-b680-3153300652eb). The ticker TSX:AGTF therefore does NOT currently represent a publicly traded, investable security — this entry in the shortlist appears to be a stale/defunct listing and should likely be removed from the live coverage universe rather than carried forward with a qualitative thesis as an active public equity.
thesis.main_shareholders: Prior to going private, Letko, Brosseau & Associates held an 18.6% stake and publicly opposed the going-private transaction as undervaluing the company [AGT announces intentions to privatize company](https://www.producer.com/?p=202134). Post-privatization, the company is controlled by the Al-Katib-led buyer group together with Fairfax Financial Holdings and Point North Capital; one unverified third-party profile also describes AGT as a Fairfax subsidiary, which is plausible but not independently confirmed here.
thesis.insider_ownership: CEO and co-founder Murad Al-Katib led the buyer group that took the company private in 2019 and remains the controlling insider/operator; co-founder Hüseyin Arslan's post-privatization stake could not be confirmed in this search.
thesis.red_flags: PRIMARY RED FLAG: the company is no longer publicly traded (delisted since April 2019); any current market data or shortlist inclusion under ticker TSX:AGTF should be treated as stale. Separately, minority shareholder Letko, Brosseau publicly objected to the going-private price as inadequate, a disclosed valuation/fairness dispute at the time of the transaction [AGT announces intentions to privatize company](https://www.producer.com/?p=202134).

name: Oil-Dri Corporation of America

thesis.business_description: Manufactures sorbent products, cat litter, and purification materials for retail, agricultural, industrial, and automotive markets
thesis.competitive_position: Oil-Dri is a niche, vertically integrated sorbent-minerals company that manufactures clay-based absorbents for pet care, fluids purification, agriculture, turf, industrial, and automotive uses, giving it exposure to specialty B2B and consumer channels rather than broad commodity markets ([Oil-Dri Corporation](https://www.oildri.com)). Its public materials emphasize proprietary mineral reserves and global production/distribution capabilities as differentiators versus other sorbent suppliers ([Oil-Dri Corporation](https://www.oildri.com)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Oil-Dri is a controlled company: Daniel S. Jaffee and the Jaffee Investment Partnership, L.P. (Jaffee family, including Chairman Richard M. Jaffee and CEO Daniel S. Jaffee) own Class B Stock representing more than 50% of aggregate voting power; exact percentage not stated in the source found ([Oil-Dri DEF 14A filings - SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/74046/000007404623000070/odcproxy2023.htm))
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources. The main business-level risk visible in company materials is dependence on specialty sorbent markets and mineral-based supply, but no material governance or accounting issues were apparent in the official sources reviewed ([Oil-Dri Corporation](https://www.oildri.com)).
thesis.insider_ownership: The Jaffee family (Richard M. Jaffee, Chairman, and Daniel S. Jaffee, President/CEO, plus siblings as general partners of the Jaffee Investment Partnership) controls more than 50% of aggregate voting power through Class B Stock, making the company a controlled company under NYSE rules ([Oil-Dri DEF 14A filings - SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/74046/000007404623000070/odcproxy2023.htm))

thesis.competitive_position: JBSS is a vertically integrated nut processor with net sales exceeding $1 billion (FY2024) and what it describes as the single largest nut-processing facility in the world; it controls procurement from growers through roasting, packaging and marketing, giving cost and quality advantages versus less-integrated peers across its three channels (consumer, commercial ingredients, contract manufacturing). thesis.main_shareholders: The Sanfilippo family controls the company through a dual-class structure in which Class A Stock carries 10 votes per share, held via multiple family trusts (e.g., Jasper B. thesis.insider_ownership: Insider/founding-family ownership is concentrated and control-dominant via the Class A super-voting shares held in Sanfilippo family trusts (Jeffrey T. Sanfilippo, Jasper B. Sanfilippo Jr., Lisa A. Sanfilippo, John E. Sanfilippo and others each hold meaningful Class A positions as trustees); the company is described as fourth-generation family-managed. Exact aggregate voting percentage was not independently confirmed in this search; see [SEC proxy filings](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000880117/000119312517285756/d436135ddef14a.htm) for the current year's beneficial ownership table.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in this search; no litigation, auditor or related-party concerns surfaced beyond the family dual-class control structure itself (which concentrates voting power but is openly disclosed in SEC filings). thesis.business_description: Graham Corporation designs and manufactures mission-critical fluid, heat-transfer, and vacuum equipment (ejectors, surface condensers, turbopumps, and rocket propulsion components) for the defense, space, petrochemical, refining, and energy industries.
thesis.competitive_position: Graham holds specialized engineering know-how in vacuum and heat-transfer equipment with a defense/space niche (including turbopumps and rocket propulsion components), positioning it as a critical, specialized supplier to a limited number of large defense/aerospace primes and industrial customers, though it is a small-cap player relative to broader industrial conglomerates.
thesis.main_shareholders: No controlling shareholder; Brandes Investment Partners is cited as the largest holder at approximately 11.3%, followed by BlackRock at ~7.02%, per Simply Wall St; the top 25 shareholders combined hold about 67.64% [Graham Corporation ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/capital-goods/nyse-ghm/graham/ownership). Institutional ownership estimates vary widely across sources (23%-83%), so should be confirmed against the latest 13F filings.
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership estimates range from roughly 0% (RedChip, likely understated/stale) to ~6.26% (Simply Wall St). Executive Chairman Daniel J. Thoren and CEO Matthew Malone hold equity-grant-based positions (reported at 374,945 and 63,629 units respectively in Form 4 filings, though undated in source) [GHM insider transactions](https://www.quantisnow.com/insiders/GHM). An open-market insider purchase by individual Mauro Gregorio (1,200 shares at ~$49.01) was reported September 12, 2025.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; no litigation, governance disputes, or auditor concerns surfaced in this search.

thesis.main_shareholders: Co-founders and insiders Romolo Magarelli (CEO/Chairman) and Douglas DeBruin are the largest shareholders, each holding approximately 32% of shares outstanding; Pembroke Management Ltd. holds about 1.5% ([Evertz Technologies Limited ownership, Simply Wall St/Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/evertz-technologies-limited-tse-et-123749577.html)).
thesis.insider_ownership: Company insiders collectively hold approximately 66% of Evertz Technologies Limited, dominated by co-founders Romolo Magarelli (~32%) and Douglas DeBruin (~32%) ([Evertz Technologies Limited ownership, Simply Wall St/Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/owning-66-evertz-technologies-limited-130226174.html)).
thesis.business_description: Evertz Technologies designs and manufactures broadcast and video infrastructure equipment (routing, production switchers, signal processing) that enables television, streaming, IPTV and mobile video content delivery.
thesis.competitive_position: Evertz is a significant global supplier of broadcast technology but is notably smaller than its chief rival Grass Valley (~$966M revenue vs. Evertz's ~$366M), also competing with Ross Video, Harmonic, EchoStar and Snell Advanced Media; it differentiates through a broad, integrated product suite for live production and routing infrastructure. [Owler](https://www.owler.com/company/evertz/competitors)
thesis.red_flags: Insider/founder control is very high: CEO Romolo Magarelli holds an estimated 25-30% of shares and director Douglas Flegher holds an estimated 15-20%, giving management tight voting control typical of founder-led companies since its 2006 IPO — a governance concentration risk for minority shareholders, though no specific lawsuit or regulatory action tied to this control was identified. Evertz has also been a plaintiff (not defendant) in patent litigation against competitor Lawo. No SEC/accounting red flags found. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/EVERTZ-TECHNOLOGIES-LIMIT-186333/company-governance/)

name: Amphastar Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

thesis.business_description: Bio-pharmaceutical company developing and selling injectable, inhalation, intranasal, and insulin API products
thesis.competitive_position: Amphastar is a specialty pharmaceutical company focused on complex injectable products, with a portfolio that includes epinephrine, naloxone, and other hospital and emergency-care medicines; its position appears to be built on difficult-to-manufacture generics and proprietary products rather than broad scale. The company competes with other generic injectable and specialty drug makers, and its niche is reflected in the mix of products and filings on its investor relations and SEC pages ([Amphastar IR](https://ir.amphastar.com), [SEC filing index](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1297184/000129718426000033/0001297184-26-000033-index.html)).
thesis.red_flags: Amphastar’s filings show ongoing reliance on a concentrated set of complex injectable products and exposure to regulatory/manufacturing execution risk typical of sterile pharmaceuticals. I did not identify a specific public filing issue from the official sources reviewed, but the company’s filings emphasize that product quality, FDA compliance, and supply continuity are material risks ([Amphastar IR](https://ir.amphastar.com), [SEC filing index](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1297184/000129718426000033/0001297184-26-000033-index.html)).
thesis.insider_ownership: Insiders own approximately 3.1% of shares outstanding; institutional investors hold approximately 55.1% ([Amphastar Pharmaceuticals ownership tracker - Benzinga/Simply Wall St](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AMPH/ownership))

industry: Healthcare / Pharmaceuticals — Bio-pharmaceutical company developing and selling injectable, inhalation, intranasal, and insulin API products

thesis.business_description: Liquidity Services operates online B2B and B2G auction marketplaces that help businesses and government agencies (including the U.S. Department of Defense) liquidate surplus, returned, and salvage inventory and equipment.
thesis.competitive_position: Liquidity Services is a long-established leader in online surplus/salvage auction marketplaces, including long-running government contracts (e.g., DoD surplus property), giving it an entrenched position in a specialized B2B/B2G reverse-logistics niche with high switching costs for government contract relationships.
thesis.main_shareholders: Co-founder William P. Angrick III (Chairman and CEO) is the largest named insider holder, described in one source as a 10% owner [Plunkett Research company profile](https://www.plunkettresearch.com/?p=1884009). Overall insider ownership is estimated at approximately 28.4% of shares per a 2025 aggregator snapshot [Liquidity Services insider selling article](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/commercial-services/nasdaq-lqdt/liquidity-services/news/dont-ignore-the-insider-selling-in-liquidity-services-1).
thesis.insider_ownership: Co-founder/CEO William Angrick holds a significant stake (10%+ per one source) though he has sold shares periodically, including a reported ~$4.7 million sale at $36.15/share that reduced his holding by only about 1.9% [Liquidity Services insider selling article](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/commercial-services/nasdaq-lqdt/liquidity-services/news/dont-ignore-the-insider-selling-in-liquidity-services-1). Director Jaime Mateus-Tique made the largest single insider sale in the trailing 12 months (~$4.9 million). Insiders were net sellers over the trailing 24 months (~456,271 shares, ~$12.97 million), with no reported insider buying in the prior 12 months.
thesis.red_flags: Sustained insider selling with no offsetting insider purchases over 24 months is worth monitoring, though it is disclosed activity and the founder/CEO retains a large stake; no litigation, auditor, or governance-dispute red flags were identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Gentherm Incorporated is a global developer and manufacturer of thermal management and pneumatic comfort technologies, best known for pioneering thermoelectric heated/cooled automotive seat systems, serving Automotive (heated/ventilated seats, steering wheels, cable systems) and Medical segments worldwide.
thesis.competitive_position: Gentherm is a global leader in automotive heated/cooled seating and thermal electronics, competing with companies such as Modine Manufacturing and Toyota Boshoku, and serves OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers seeking advanced thermal comfort and lean manufacturing capabilities [company overview aggregation](https://www.zoominfo.com/c/gentherm-inc/348755325); Gentherm is credited with creating the first thermoelectrically heated and cooled automotive seat system.
thesis.main_shareholders: Ownership is predominantly institutional with no controlling shareholder: Vanguard Group (~11.5%, as of a 2023 filing) and BlackRock Inc. (~15.96%, as of a late-2022 filing) have historically been the largest holders, alongside State Street, Geode Capital Management, BNY Mellon, and Loomis Sayles; more current 2025/2026 percentage breakdowns were not available in the sources reviewed, but no founder-family control was identified [SEC-filing-sourced holder data via WebSearch](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/903129/000114036125010582/ny20041334x1_def14a.pdf). Note: some aggregator sites returned apparently stale/inconsistent insider-holder percentages (e.g., figures resembling pre-2010 Amerigon-era ownership); those figures were not used here due to reliability concerns.
thesis.insider_ownership: Corporate insiders collectively own approximately 2.1% of the company; CEO Phillip M. Eyler holds roughly 147,317 shares directly, with no evidence of founder-family control in current ownership [WallStreetZen ownership data](https://www.wallstreetzen.com/stocks/us/nasdaq/thrm/ownership).
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in available search results.

thesis.business_description: Mission Produce is a global grower, packer, and distributor of fresh avocados (and expanding into mangoes), sourcing from company-owned and partner farms across Latin America and operating ripening/distribution facilities to supply retail and food-service customers worldwide.
thesis.competitive_position: Mission Produce is one of the largest vertically integrated avocado companies globally, with owned farms, packing facilities, and a global distribution network spanning multiple growing regions (giving it year-round supply diversification versus smaller single-region avocado suppliers), though the business remains exposed to commodity price volatility and weather/crop-yield risk.
thesis.main_shareholders: Individual insiders are the largest ownership bloc at approximately 35% per a February 2025 Simply Wall St analysis; Bruce Taylor is named as the single largest shareholder at approximately 12%, with the top 11 shareholders together holding about 51% [Mission Produce insider ownership article](https://www.itiger.com/news/2508133667). Taylor Family Investments, LLC appears as a 10%+ owner in insider-transaction records, though its relation to any founding family is unconfirmed in this search.
thesis.insider_ownership: CEO Stephen Barnard is named as a top-three shareholder and sits on the board, per the same Simply Wall St analysis [Mission Produce insider ownership article](https://www.itiger.com/news/2508133667). Insiders were net sellers over an 18-month tracking window (2,688,185 shares sold, 0 bought, per one aggregator), while Globalharvest Holdings Venture Ltd. appears as a frequent buyer in Form 4 filings, though its affiliation is unconfirmed.
thesis.red_flags: Notable insider selling with no offsetting buying over 18 months (per one tracker) is worth monitoring; no litigation, auditor, or governance-dispute red flags were identified from official sources.

name: Cascades Inc.

thesis.business_description: Sustainable packaging, tissue, and recycled-fibre recovery products across North America
thesis.competitive_position: Cascades positions itself as a North American supplier of sustainable, value-added packaging, hygiene and recovery solutions, with operations spanning 60 production units and a recycling heritage that supports its recycled-containerboard and tissue businesses. Its niche is narrower than diversified peers like WestRock/Smurfit Kappa or International Paper, but its focus on eco-friendly packaging and recycled fiber products gives it a differentiated position in Canada and U.S. regional markets ([Cascades news](https://www.cascades.com/en/news/cascades-reports-shareholders-voting-results-election-directors-11), [Cascades investor relations](https://www.cascades.com/en/investors)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Not disclosed in public filings
thesis.red_flags: Recent company commentary points to weaker packaging volumes, higher transportation/fuel costs, and execution inefficiencies, and management lowered its Q1 2026 EBITDA outlook versus prior guidance. The company also flagged broader risks from demand softness, raw-material costs, currency moves, and adverse industry conditions in its forward-looking statements ([Cascades news](https://www.cascades.com/en/news/cascades-release-first-quarter-2026-financial-results-may-7-2026-provides-updated-outlook)).

industry: Materials / Packaging — Sustainable packaging, tissue, and recycled-fibre recovery products across North America

thesis.main_shareholders: As of the FY2025 proxy: BlackRock, Inc. held 13.0% (6,899,719 shares) and The Vanguard Group held 8.7% (4,628,200 shares). Note: Apollo Global Management affiliate SCA Horus Holdings, LLC (formerly a major shareholder post-2018 acquisition) has since fully exited its position ([Sun Country Airlines DEF 14A FY2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1743907/000119312525097007/d824709ddef14a.htm))
thesis.business_description: Sun Country Airlines Holdings operates a hybrid airline model combining scheduled leisure passenger service, passenger charter flying, and contract air cargo operations (notably for Amazon Air) using Boeing 737 aircraft.
thesis.competitive_position: Sun Country differentiates from both network carriers and pure ultra-low-cost carriers by dynamically allocating aircraft across three revenue streams - scheduled (~68% of revenue), charter (~17%), and cargo (~15%) - to maximize aircraft utilization and smooth seasonality; its cargo business flies Boeing 737-800 freighters under a six-year Amazon Air agreement (through 2030) that has grown from 12 to 20+ aircraft.
