[Digiday](https://digiday.com/marketing/1-800-flowers-competes-direct-consumer-era/)
thesis.red_flags: Significant red flag: law firm Kaplan Fox announced a securities-law investigation (May 2025) alleging that 1-800-Flowers and management issued overly optimistic FY2025 guidance and positive public statements (May 3-8, 2024) that proved misleading; the stock fell over 33% intraday on May 9, 2025 upon related disclosures. Founder James F. McCann stepped down as CEO around this period (remaining Executive Chairman), a leadership change coinciding with the controversy. McCann's founder-control legacy (built the company from a single NYC flower shop starting 1976) also means significant insider influence over governance. [NewMediaWire](https://www.newmediawire.com/news/kaplan-fox-announces-an-investigation-into-1-800-flowers-com-inc-for-potential-securities-law-violations-7080661)

thesis.business_description: Gencor Industries, Inc. is an Orlando, Florida-based manufacturer of highway and heavy equipment, specializing in asphalt plants and related equipment used in road construction, as well as combustion/drying equipment.
thesis.competitive_position: Gencor is a small, niche manufacturer of asphalt production equipment with a long operating history; it is tightly controlled by the Elliott family through a dual-class share structure (Common and Class B stock), with Class B holders electing 75% of the board. [GENCOR INDUSTRIES INC Schedule 13D FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000064472/000110465926057949/primary_doc.xml).
thesis.main_shareholders: The Elliott Family Limited Partnership, now controlled by Marc G. Elliott after a May 2026 gift transfer of membership interests from his father E.J. Elliott, held 1,518,828 common shares (12.3%) and 2,022,477 Class B shares (87.2%) as of February 5, 2026; combined with his personal holdings, Marc Elliott's reported position totals roughly 27.3% of total shares outstanding. [GENCOR INDUSTRIES INC Schedule 13D FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000064472/000110465926057949/primary_doc.xml); [Gencor Industries 8-K FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000064472/000119312526212435/d143818d8k.htm).
thesis.insider_ownership: Family/insider control is very high and concentrated via the dual-class structure: as of the June 2025 proxy, E.J. Elliott held ~13.3% of common and ~87.9% of Class B stock (before the May 2026 gift transfer to son Marc Elliott); all directors/executive officers as a group held 2,145,303 common shares and 2,318,857 Class B shares. [Gencor Industries FY2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/64472/000119312525150836/d877455d10k.htm).
thesis.red_flags: The company has a dual-class voting structure concentrating board control (75% of directors) in Class B stock held almost entirely (~95%) by the Elliott family, and a May 2026 intra-family gift transfer shifted voting control from E.J. Elliott to his son Marc Elliott with no cash consideration -- a governance structure that materially limits minority shareholder influence, though not itself an allegation of wrongdoing. [GENCOR INDUSTRIES INC Schedule 13D FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000064472/000110465926057949/primary_doc.xml).

name: Immersion Corporation

thesis.business_description: Licenses haptic touch-feedback software and IP for mobile, gaming, automotive, and medical devices
thesis.competitive_position: Immersion is a niche haptic-technology licensor and solutions provider focused on touch feedback for mobile, automotive, gaming, and other consumer experiences; its site says it builds “touch experiences in the digital world” and works with device manufacturers, haptic hardware companies, designers, developers, and ecosystem partners ([Immersion](https://www.immersion.com/)).
thesis.main_shareholders: William Martin is a top shareholder with approximately 7.3% of shares outstanding; other large holders include stakes of approximately 7.2% and 5.6% (specific names/dates not fully disclosed in the source found) ([Immersion Corp ownership structure - Nasdaq](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/heres-what-immersion-corporations-nasdaq:immr-shareholder-ownership-structure-looks-like))
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.
thesis.insider_ownership: Director Eric Singer held approximately 5.5% of shares (1,826,961 shares) as of August 2026, after holding 6.8% (2,235,922 shares) in March 2026 and 2.3% (743,425 shares) in March 2024; William Martin held approximately 2.7% (859,691 shares) as of March 2024 ([Immersion Corp DEF 14A FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1058811/000119312526374299/immr-20260828.htm))

industry: Technology / Semiconductors — Licenses haptic touch-feedback software and IP for mobile, gaming, automotive, and medical devices

name: SWK Holdings Corporation

thesis.business_description: Building systems solutions for mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and controls infrastructure
thesis.competitive_position: SWK Holdings Corporation is a specialty finance company that originates and invests in asset-based and specialty loans, which puts it in a niche lending segment rather than a broad commercial bank model, as described in its SEC filings. Its competition comes from other specialty finance and asset-based lenders that can underwrite smaller, more complex credits, while its portfolio structure and underwriting focus differentiate it from traditional bank lenders.
thesis.red_flags: The main risk is concentration: as a specialty lender, performance depends on a relatively small number of borrowers and collateral positions, which can magnify losses if credits deteriorate. SEC filings also indicate the company has active ownership/insider Form 4 activity, but no specific governance or accounting red flag was identified from the official sources reviewed.

industry: Industrials / Engineering & Construction — Building systems solutions for mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and controls infrastructure

thesis.business_description: Clarke Inc. is a Halifax, Nova Scotia-based investment holding company that allocates capital into operating businesses and real assets across Canada — including real estate/investment properties, a ferry business, loan receivables, and a hospitality segment (hotel ownership/management) — targeting undervalued or underperforming companies and assets.
thesis.competitive_position: Clarke functions as a hybrid private-equity-style investor/operator rather than a company with a product moat; its 'edge' is CEO/Chairman George Armoyan's track record as an activist/value investor deploying equity and debt into distressed or mispriced assets (e.g., recently acquiring hotel owner/operator Holloway Lodging and bailing out Ravelin). See [company profile](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/tsx/CKI/company/) and [Koneko Research analysis](https://www.konekoresearch.com/p/clarke-inc-value-compounder-just).
thesis.main_shareholders: Extremely concentrated control: George Armoyan (CEO and Chairman) and his family, via G2S2 Capital Inc., hold a majority stake; aggregator data shows Armoyan individually/beneficially holding approximately 85.46% of shares (~11,082,300 shares, ~$205M value as of March 30, 2026). Source: [MarketScreener insider data](https://www.marketscreener.com/insider/GEORGE-ARMOYAN-A047YB/).
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is effectively controlling at ~85% via George Armoyan/G2S2 Capital/family (including reported purchases by 'Sime Armoyan', a family member); this is a founder/controlling-shareholder situation with very limited free float and low trading liquidity. Sources: [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/insider/GEORGE-ARMOYAN-A047YB/), [CanadianInsider on Sime Armoyan buying](https://www.canadianinsider.com/money-moving/2020-03-12/sime-armoyan-buying-clarke-cki).
thesis.red_flags: Significant related-party-transaction and governance risk given ~85% insider control: in the Ravelin transaction, George Armoyan's family office reportedly held secured debt in the target and was able to dictate restructuring terms in a way that wiped out equity holders, and in the Holloway Lodging transaction Armoyan and other Clarke directors had to abstain from voting due to conflicts of interest. Trading liquidity is low given the concentrated float. These are structural conflict-of-interest risks inherent to a closely-controlled holding company, not an SEC enforcement action, but warrant caution. Sources: [Bullpen Finance on Ravelin deal](https://www.bullpen.finance/p/clarke-bails-out-ravelin-in-1-1b-deal), [RENX on Holloway Lodging acquisition](https://renx.ca/clarke-acquire-hotel-owner-operator-holloway-lodging). Note: George Armoyan announced he would step down as CEO per a 2026 news report — a leadership transition to monitor. Source: [RTTNews](https://www.rttnews.com/2336367/clarke-inc-ceo-george-armoyan-to-step-down.aspx?Arch=1).

name: Electromed, Inc.

thesis.business_description: Designs and sells airway clearance therapy systems for patients with chronic lung conditions
thesis.competitive_position: Electromed is a niche respiratory device company centered on the SmartVest high-frequency chest wall oscillation (HFCWO) airway-clearance system for bronchiectasis, COPD, and related chronic lung conditions. Its position appears differentiated by a focused product line and long-standing specialization in HFCWO, competing in a category that includes larger respiratory-device players such as Hillrom/Baxter and AffloVest/Tactile Medical-adjacent airway-clearance offerings, while its own site emphasizes SmartVest as the only brand singularly dedicated to HFCWO therapy.
thesis.main_shareholders: Former director Stephen H. Craney has remained a beneficial owner of greater than 5% of outstanding common stock through at least June 30, 2025 (exact current percentage not disclosed in the source found); historically (FY2014 proxy) Thomas M. Hagedorn held 9.8% (793,108 shares), Craig N. Hansen held 5.8% (473,180 shares), and Craney held 5.7% ([Electromed DEF 14A filings - SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1488917/000143774925030113/elmd20250919_def14a.htm))
thesis.red_flags: The company is highly concentrated in a single product category and therapy type, which leaves it exposed to reimbursement, adoption, and competitive pressures in airway clearance. Official sources also show a small-cap, single-business model with no obvious diversification, so execution risk is elevated if SmartVest demand softens.

industry: Healthcare / Medical Devices — Designs and sells airway clearance therapy systems for patients with chronic lung conditions

thesis.business_description: Merchants' National Properties, Inc. is a New York City-based real estate company that acquires, develops, operates, manages and leases commercial real estate, primarily shopping centers and office buildings, with interests in dozens of properties across multiple US states.
thesis.competitive_position: The company holds fractional/joint ownership interests (rather than full ownership) in many of its properties, including a reported 37.6% interest in the Cross Country Center shopping complex in Yonkers, NY as of 2022; it is a small, closely-held, thinly-traded real estate holding company tracing its roots to 1815/1928 incorporation, operating through subsidiary Marx Realty & Improvement, Inc. (acquired 2006). [Merchants National Properties writeup - Value Investors Club](https://valueinvestorsclub.com/idea/MERCHANTS_NATIONAL_PPTYS_INC/0281927459).
thesis.main_shareholders: A 2022 Value Investors Club analysis described the company as effectively controlled by the founding families, who do not always share aligned goals; current percentage stakes were not found via aggregator sites, which showed no usable top-holder data. [Merchants National Properties writeup - Value Investors Club](https://valueinvestorsclub.com/idea/MERCHANTS_NATIONAL_PPTYS_INC/0281927459).
thesis.insider_ownership: Not disclosed in public filings found in this search; described only qualitatively (founding-family control) in a third-party investor write-up rather than with sourced percentages. [Merchants National Properties writeup - Value Investors Club](https://valueinvestorsclub.com/idea/MERCHANTS_NATIONAL_PPTYS_INC/0281927459).
thesis.red_flags: A 2022 investor write-up noted that the controlling founding families do not always pursue the same goals, implying potential family governance friction, though this is one investor's characterization rather than an official disclosure. [Merchants National Properties writeup - Value Investors Club](https://valueinvestorsclub.com/idea/MERCHANTS_NATIONAL_PPTYS_INC/0281927459).

thesis.business_description: Motorcar Parts of America, Inc. remanufactures and distributes aftermarket auto parts — alternators, starters, wheel hub assemblies/bearings, brake calipers/rotors/pads, turbochargers — plus heavy-duty truck, industrial, marine and agricultural replacement parts, selling through major retail chains (AutoZone, Advance Auto Parts, O'Reilly, Genuine Parts).
thesis.competitive_position: MPAA is a major remanufacturer in the North American rotating-electrical and brake-parts aftermarket, with scaled production (8.8M+ units annual capacity) across U.S., Mexico, Malaysia and Singapore facilities; remanufacturing offers a cost/sustainability edge (up to ~91% less material/energy than new manufacturing) versus OEM-new parts, but the business is a relatively commoditized category with large-retailer customer concentration. See [company history](https://motorcarparts.com/company/history/).
thesis.main_shareholders: No controlling shareholder; largest holder is Private Capital Management, LLC (~13%), with 325 Capital LLC, Pacific Ridge Capital Partners, Donald Smith & Co. (~6.54% per 13G), Dimensional Fund Advisors, Vanguard, Tieton Capital Management and Azarias Capital Management also holding stakes; institutions hold ~70% overall. Source: [StockTitan 13G filing](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/MPAA/schedule-13g-motorcar-parts-of-america-inc-passive-investment-disclos-559e36391259.html).
thesis.insider_ownership: Chairman/CEO Selwyn Joffe holds approximately 2.6% of shares; collective insider holdings are reported at roughly US$15M against a ~US$226M market cap. Source: [Yahoo Finance ownership article](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/70-ownership-motorcar-parts-america-113245298.html).
thesis.red_flags: SIGNIFICANT HISTORICAL RED FLAG: Motorcar Parts of America (then Motorcar Parts & Accessories) was the subject of an SEC enforcement action and DOJ criminal charges for accounting fraud in fiscal 1997-1998 (overstating pre-tax earnings by 59.8% and 49.6% in those years via manipulated returned-product/credit reserves); then-COO Richard Marks (son of the founder) and then-CFO Peter Bromberg were criminally convicted and jailed, and the auditor withdrew its audit opinions on those years. Separately, in 2006 the company restated financials due to a settlement-agreement accounting error, partly prompted by SEC Corp Fin comments, and after its 2011 acquisition of Fenwick Automotive Products (Fenco) under current CEO Selwyn Joffe, MPAA discovered Fenco's inventory accounting had been fraudulent. Given this multi-decade pattern of accounting problems (though the most severe fraud predates current management), this is a name requiring elevated scrutiny of financial statement quality. Sources: [SEC v. Motorcar Parts and Accessories complaint](https://www.sec.gov/litigation/complaints/comp17736.htm), [Seeking Alpha on accounting history](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4289805-motorcar-parts-of-america-history-of-accounting-fraud-earnings-look-overstated-solvency).

thesis.business_description: InfuSystem Holdings, Inc. is a leading provider of ambulatory infusion pumps and related services (rental equipment plus disposable supply kits) to hospitals, oncology practices, surgery centers and other alternate-site providers, with its Integrated Therapy Services platform spanning oncology (~90% of Patient Services revenue), pain management, wound therapy and lymphedema.
thesis.competitive_position: InfuSystem is described as a leading provider in ambulatory infusion pump rental/service with a large device fleet (100,000+ mobile medical devices) and multiple U.S./Canada 'Centers of Excellence,' giving it scale advantages in a niche, recurring-revenue DME rental model tied to oncology treatment protocols. See [primer](https://shareholdersunite.substack.com/p/a-primer-on-infusystem) and [IR site](https://ir.infusystem.com/).
thesis.main_shareholders: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are investment managers Minerva Advisors LLC (~5.97%, also the largest hedge fund holder), Acuitas Investments (~5.10%), Sansone Advisors (~4.65%), Vanguard (~4.26%) and Punch & Associates (~4.09%); institutions overall hold ~82% and hedge funds collectively ~19%. Source: [TradingKey shareholder structure](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/infu/ownership).
thesis.insider_ownership: Insiders collectively hold about 11.4% of shares; CEO Richard DiIorio holds approximately 0.9% individually. Source: [aggregator insider ownership data](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/kind-shareholders-hold-majority-infusystem-075025447.html).
thesis.red_flags: Historical accounting issue: InfuSystem restated its FY2015 financial statements and Q1-Q2 2016 interim results after identifying errors related to overstated estimated accounts-receivable collections; this led to a securities class action (filed Nov. 2016 against the company, then-CEO Eric Steen and then-CFO Jonathan Foster) alleging materially false/misleading SEC disclosures, which was dismissed with prejudice in January 2018 (plaintiff failed to amend the complaint), plus a related shareholder derivative suit settled in December 2018 with governance-change commitments. These are legacy (2015-2018) issues; no more recent accounting or litigation red flags were found. Sources: [InfuSystem press release on class action dismissal](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/infusystem-holdings-inc-announces-dismissal-of-class-action-shareholder-lawsuit-300591437.html), [derivative lawsuit settlement release](https://ir.infusystem.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1282/infusystem-holdings-inc-announces-settlement-of).

thesis.business_description: Anika Therapeutics, Inc. develops, manufactures and commercializes joint-preservation and orthobiologics products built on proprietary hyaluronic-acid technology — including osteoarthritis pain injections (Monovisc, Orthovisc), cartilage-repair/regenerative products (Hyalofast, TactoSet) and sports-medicine implants/instrumentation (via its Arthrosurface and Parcus Medical acquisitions) — plus dermal, surgical and ophthalmic HA-based products.
thesis.competitive_position: Anika is a small-cap (FY2025 revenue ~$112.8M, down 6% YoY) specialty orthopedic medtech company with a long-standing franchise in hyaluronic-acid viscosupplementation, which it has been diversifying into sports medicine/joint-restoration via acquisitions; gross margin expanded to 63% in FY2025 on favorable mix, but overall revenue has been declining, indicating competitive/reimbursement pressure in its legacy OA-injection business. See [FY2025 results](https://ir.anika.com/Anika-Therapeutics-Reports-Record-First-Quarter-Revenue-and-Earnings) and [company profile](https://umbrex.com/resources/company-profiles/anika-therapeutics/).
thesis.main_shareholders: No controlling shareholder; activist fund Caligan Partners LP took a stake and pushed for board changes starting February 2023, leading to a Cooperation Agreement (April 2023) expanding the board to eight directors and adding an independent director (Gary Fischetti); Caligan nominated additional director candidates again in March 2024, indicating sustained activist involvement. Specific current percentage stakes were not confirmed in this search. Source: [TipRanks on CEO/governance changes](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/anika-therapeutics-announces-ceo-transition-and-governance-changes).
thesis.insider_ownership: Not independently quantified in this search; governance has been materially reshaped by the Caligan activist campaign and a January 2026 leadership transition (CFO/COO Stephen Griffin became President & CEO effective Feb 1, 2026, succeeding Cheryl R. Blanchard, who moved to Executive Chair) rather than by a traditional founder/family ownership block.
thesis.red_flags: Multiple recent red flags: (1) activist pressure from Caligan Partners resulted in board turnover (2023-2024); (2) a abrupt CEO transition announced January 2026; (3) following disappointing July 30, 2025 topline results from the pivotal U.S. Hyalofast cartilage-repair trial, the stock fell over 27% in a single day, prompting at least one law firm to open an investigation into potential securities-law violations (status of any filed suit not confirmed). These together suggest elevated governance and clinical/commercial-execution risk. Sources: [OrthoSpineNews on leadership transition](https://orthospinenews.com/2026/01/08/anika-therapeutics-announces-leadership-transition/), [ZLK class-action case page](https://zlk.com/cases/anika-therapeutics-inc-class-action-lawsuit-anik).

thesis.insider_ownership: CEO Mario Gabelli directly owns approximately 28.95% of LICT Corporation shares ([LICT Corporation company profile - CB Insights/Simply Wall St](https://www.cbinsights.com/company/lict-corporation/people))
thesis.business_description: LICT Corporation is a holding company whose subsidiaries provide integrated broadband internet, voice (VoIP/wireless), and video/cable television services to residential and business customers in rural markets across several U.S. states, plus TV broadcasting in Illinois and Iowa.
thesis.competitive_position: LICT is a small, thinly-traded (OTC Pink) roll-up of independent rural telephone/cable companies (owning roughly 7,483 miles of fiber, 8,945 miles of copper and 847 miles of coax, plus 103 towers and 301 spectrum licenses) that continues to make small tuck-in acquisitions, such as Manti Telephone Company in 2023; it competes as a niche rural incumbent telco/cable operator in markets too small to attract national carriers. [LICT Corporation](https://www.lictcorp.com/) / [Manti acquisition announcement](https://lictcorp.com/2023/10/05/lict-corporation-announces-acquisition-of-manti-telephone-company/)
thesis.red_flags: LICT has long been effectively controlled by GAMCO/Mario Gabelli-affiliated interests (a director and major shareholder), trades on OTC Pink with minimal liquidity, analyst coverage, and abbreviated public disclosure compared to exchange-listed peers; no specific litigation, auditor, or fraud allegation was found in available searches, but the controlled-company structure and thin float are worth monitoring. [LICT Corporation Annual Report](https://www.otcmarkets.com/file/company/financial-report/402422/content)

name: ADF Group Inc.

thesis.business_description: North American fabrication and installation of complex steel superstructures for non-residential infrastructure projects
thesis.competitive_position: ADF Group positions itself as a North American leader in complex steel structures and heavy steel components, with annual fabrication capacity of about 125,000 tonnes and integrated engineering, detailing, fabrication, coating, and installation services. Its niche is large, highly complex projects rather than commodity structural steel, competing in the broader fabricated structural steel market against firms such as Canam Group and Walters Group. [ADF Group website](https://www.adfgroup.com) [ADF Group Investors](https://www.adfgroup.com/en/investors)
thesis.main_shareholders: Insiders collectively hold approximately 29% of ADF Group Inc.; the largest individual holders reported are Pierre Paschini (President), Jean Paschini (CEO) and Les Placements G. Maps Inc., each cited at roughly 14% of shares outstanding ([ADF Group Inc. ownership, Simply Wall St/Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/adf-group-inc-tse-drx-124936952.html)).
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources. The main business risk evident from official materials is project/construction execution dependence, but no specific regulatory, accounting, or governance red flags were identified in the sources reviewed. [ADF Group website](https://www.adfgroup.com) [ADF Group Investors](https://www.adfgroup.com/en/investors)
thesis.insider_ownership: Individual insiders account for approximately 29% of ADF Group Inc.'s shares outstanding ([ADF Group Inc. ownership, Simply Wall St/Yahoo Finance](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/adf-group-inc-tse-drx-152110342.html)).

industry: Materials / Construction Materials — North American fabrication and installation of complex steel superstructures for non-residential infrastructure projects

name: Andrew Peller Limited

thesis.business_description: Produces and markets wines, spirits, ciders, seltzers, and home winemaking products in Canada.
thesis.competitive_position: Andrew Peller Limited positions itself as Canada’s largest premium wine producer, with a portfolio that includes Peller Estates, Trius, and Wayne Gretzky, plus spirits, beer, cider, seltzers, and wine-tourism properties. Its niche is a branded Canadian premium beverage platform with winery/tourism assets, competing against large beverage alcohol players such as Constellation Brands and Corby/Arterra-style domestic wine peers rather than commodity wine producers.
thesis.main_shareholders: The Peller founding family (John Peller and Peller Family Enterprises Inc.) is the controlling shareholder group, holding voting control primarily through Class B multiple-voting shares; John Peller serves as Executive Chairman ([Andrew Peller Limited ownership structure, Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/food-beverage-tobacco/otc-adwp.f/andrew-peller/ownership)). Note: Andrew Peller announced a definitive agreement to be acquired by Fairfax Financial in 2026, ending the family's public-company ownership.
thesis.red_flags: The company notes exposure to competitive pressures, changing consumer preferences, and other operating risks typical of beverage alcohol and hospitality businesses; however, the official sources reviewed did not identify a specific material accounting or governance red flag. None identified from official sources beyond ordinary business risks.
thesis.insider_ownership: Company insiders own approximately 32% of the company (worth about CA$59 million), concentrated in the Peller family's Class B share holdings ([Andrew Peller Limited ownership structure, Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/food-beverage-tobacco/otc-adwp.f/andrew-peller/ownership)).

industry: Consumer Staples / Beverages — Produces and markets wines, spirits, ciders, seltzers, and home winemaking products in Canada.

name: Pulse Seismic Inc.

thesis.business_description: Provider of 2D and 3D seismic data acquisition, licensing, and project services in western Canada
thesis.competitive_position: Pulse Seismic says it owns and manages Canada’s largest licensable seismic data library, covering the Western Canada Sedimentary Basin and other regions, which gives it a niche as a data-licensing provider to oil and gas explorers rather than an upstream producer ([Pulse Seismic Investor Overview](https://pulseseismic.com/investors/investor-overview/)). Its position is tied to the size, quality, and repeat-licensing value of that proprietary library, which the company describes as an industry-leading asset ([Pulse Seismic Investor Overview](https://pulseseismic.com/investors/investor-overview/)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Institutional investors collectively own more than half of Pulse Seismic Inc.'s issued shares; specific named institutional holders and their individual percentages were not found in available sources ([Pulse Seismic Inc. shareholder composition, Simply Wall St/Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/kind-shareholders-own-pulse-seismic-143912697.html)).
thesis.red_flags: The main business concentration risk is heavy exposure to western Canadian energy exploration activity, so demand for seismic data can weaken if oil and gas drilling and development slow ([Pulse Seismic Investor Overview](https://pulseseismic.com/investors/investor-overview/)). No material governance or accounting issues were identified from the official investor overview page reviewed ([Pulse Seismic Investor Overview](https://pulseseismic.com/investors/investor-overview/)).
thesis.insider_ownership: Company insiders collectively hold approximately CA$1.3 million of the roughly CA$78 million company (on the order of 1-2% by value); Pulse Seismic is not owned by hedge funds ([Pulse Seismic Inc. shareholder composition, Simply Wall St/Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/kind-shareholders-own-pulse-seismic-143912697.html)).

industry: Energy / Oil & Gas Equipment & Services — Provider of 2D and 3D seismic data acquisition, licensing, and project services in western Canada

name: Methode Electronics, Inc.

thesis.business_description: Designs and manufactures custom electronic components and systems for transportation, industrial, and medical end markets
thesis.competitive_position: Methode Electronics is a niche supplier of custom-engineered electronic components and subsystems, with SEC filings identifying it as an electronic connectors business (SIC 3678) and its investor materials emphasizing automotive, industrial, and infrastructure applications. Its position depends on design-in relationships and customer-specific engineering, competing with larger interconnect and electronics component makers such as TE Connectivity, Amphenol, and Molex rather than on broad commodity volume. [SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65270/000166430126000007/0001664301-26-000007-index.htm)
thesis.main_shareholders: Not disclosed in public filings
thesis.red_flags: SEC filings show the company has had recent delinquent filing issues: Methode’s investor relations site listed a current report filing in May 2026, but the latest annual report/proxy were not readily surfaced in the official materials I reviewed. The company also carries the usual concentration risk typical of a custom-component supplier, with dependence on a limited number of OEM and industrial customers and cyclical end markets. [Methode IR filings](https://ir.methode.com/financials/sec-filings/default.aspx), [SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65270/000166430126000007/0001664301-26-000007-index.htm)

industry: Technology / Electronic Components — Designs and manufactures custom electronic components and systems for transportation, industrial, and medical end markets

name: inTEST Corporation

thesis.business_description: Test and process equipment for semiconductor, automotive, and industrial manufacturing applications
thesis.competitive_position: inTEST Corporation is a niche supplier of test and handling equipment used in semiconductor and other electronics manufacturing, and its positioning rests on specialized thermal, motion, and test-interface products rather than broad-scale volume manufacturing. Its SEC filings identify the company as an instruments-for-measurement-and-testing business, with competition in the broader semiconductor test-equipment market from companies such as Teradyne and other niche equipment suppliers.
thesis.main_shareholders: Not disclosed in public filings

thesis.competitive_position: American Vanguard is a mid/small-cap specialty agrochemical company focused on niche, often off-patent crop-protection products; its market capitalization and stock have fallen sharply (to roughly $64.75 million by August 2026 from about $700 million at the time of a 2022 proxy fight), coinciding with weak earnings and a contested governance period. [Insider trading alert - InsiderTrades.com](https://www.insidertrades.com/alerts/nyse-avd-insider-buying-and-selling-2026-08-19/).
thesis.main_shareholders: Historical ownership by the founding Wintemute family has declined over time: Glenn Wintemute held ~25.6% in 1997, falling to ~8.2% by 2005 and ~4.9% by 2009; a 2014 proxy showed Eric Wintemute (long-time CEO/Chairman) at ~4.7% individually with directors/officers as a group at ~5.9% (current figures should be reverified). [American Vanguard DEF 14A FY2014](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000005981/000119312514154868/d699851ddef14a.htm).
thesis.insider_ownership: Eric Wintemute served as CEO since 1994 and Chairman since 2011, with a reported ~4.7% personal stake as of the 2014 proxy (likely diluted further since); he stepped down as CEO per a 2024 transition agreement, with his board term ending at the 2025 annual meeting, followed by an April 2025 cooperation agreement requiring him to withdraw a board nomination and accept standstill terms. [American Vanguard DEF 14A FY2014](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000005981/000119312514154868/d699851ddef14a.htm).
thesis.red_flags: Significant governance turmoil: in 2022, activist Cruiser Capital (~2.5% holder) won three board seats after alleging a 'persistent record of underperformance and governance failures,' with proxy advisor Glass Lewis siding against management; CEO/Chairman Eric Wintemute subsequently transitioned out of the CEO role (2024) and agreed to standstill terms (April 2025). Separately, subsidiary AMVAC faced EPA enforcement action (Notice of Intent to Suspend its DCPA/Dacthal pesticide registration, April 2022; suspended by an administrative judge in July 2022, later remanded for a hearing by the EPA's Environmental Appeals Board) and related product-liability lawsuits; a plaintiff law firm (Berger Montague) has also publicized an investigation into potential board fiduciary-duty breaches. Market cap has fallen roughly 90% from 2022 to August 2026. [American vanguard fights proxy battle - OCBJ](https://www.ocbj.com/finance/american-vanguard-fights-proxy-battle/); [Chemical Week - activist wins three board seats](https://chemweek.mydigitalpublication.com/articles/activist-wins-three-seats-on-american-vanguard-board); [EPA DCPA administrative docket](https://yosemite.epa.gov/oarm/ALJ/ALJ_Web_Docket.nsf/All+Content+-+Web/51184B12B88D777A8525886A005DD7F8).

thesis.business_description: America's Car-Mart, Inc. is an integrated used-vehicle retailer and finance company operating roughly 154 'buy-here-pay-here' dealerships across 12 South-Central U.S. states, selling older-model used vehicles directly to credit-challenged consumers and financing the purchases itself (earning interest income and fees) rather than relying on third-party lenders.
thesis.competitive_position: Car-Mart is among the largest publicly traded 'integrated' (sell-and-finance) used-car retailers focused exclusively on the deep-subprime/non-prime customer segment in small Southern/Midwestern towns; its historical moat was underwriting expertise and direct customer relationships, but the model is capital-intensive and highly sensitive to credit performance of its loan book. See [company profile](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/crmt/company/).
thesis.main_shareholders: No controlling shareholder; largest holders include The Magnolia Group, LLC (~15.18%), Adam K. Peterson (~12.93%, 1,119,875 shares, though he has been selling — a June 2025 transaction left him with 1,516,094 shares per one report, figures vary by date), Jonathan Z. Buba (~7.91%), Nantahala Capital Management (~7.76%) and Prescott Group Capital Management (~7.23%). Institutions hold ~29.5% and insiders ~23.35% overall. Source: [TipRanks ownership data](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crmt/ownership).
thesis.insider_ownership: Insiders collectively hold roughly 23.35% of shares per aggregator data, concentrated among a small number of large individual holders (Peterson, Buba) rather than company executives; a major shareholder reportedly sold ~$294.1M in stock per a June 2025 MarketBeat alert, a significant insider liquidity event to note. Source: [MarketBeat major shareholder sale alert](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/americas-car-mart-inc-nasdaqcrmt-major-shareholder-sells-294097000-in-stock-2025-06-11).
thesis.red_flags: SIGNIFICANT ACTIVE RED FLAGS: (1) Car-Mart disclosed a footnote on loan modifications/bad-loan issues that, despite being characterized as having 'no material impact on earnings,' preceded an 18.2% single-day stock drop (Sept. 4, 2025) on rising delinquencies and ultimately contributed to the closure of roughly 42 dealerships (about a third of its footprint); (2) the company has warned of going-concern/severe liquidity and debt risk in SEC filings and was operating under temporary covenant relief/waivers (initially expiring Sept. 7, 2026, with conditional extensions to Nov. 6, 2026); (3) the Rosen Law Firm and others are actively investigating/soliciting a securities class action alleging materially misleading disclosures. This is a current, high-severity financial-distress and disclosure-adequacy situation requiring close monitoring — potentially disqualifying for a conservative value shortlist pending resolution. Sources: [Yahoo Finance/The Auto Wire on buried footnote](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/americas-car-mart-buried-footnote-020000502.html), [StockTitan on going-concern warning](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CRMT/ars-americas-carmart-inc-sec-filing-13d61811b0a3.html), [GlobeNewswire Rosen Law Firm investor alert](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/29/3371303/673/en/crmt-investor-news-if-you-have-suffered-losses-in-america-s-car-mart-inc-nasdaq-crmt-you-are-encouraged-to-contact-the-rosen-law-firm-about-your-rights.html).

name: Medifast, Inc.

thesis.business_description: Direct-to-consumer metabolic health company selling coach-guided weight management plans and scientifically developed nutrition products
thesis.competitive_position: Medifast is a niche metabolic health and wellness company built around its coach-guided OPTAVIA system, with science-backed products, personalized plans, and a network of independent coaches. Its positioning is differentiated by that direct-to-consumer, coach-led model, but the company itself says it faces competition from GLP-1 weight-loss medications and other weight-loss products/services, and it is trying to pivot toward metabolic health. ([Medifast IR](https://ir.medifastinc.com/news/news-details/2026/Medifast-Announces-First-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx), [Medifast homepage](https://www.medifastinc.com/))
thesis.main_shareholders: As of April 21, 2025: Renaissance Technologies LLC owned 9.2% (1,006,210 shares), BlackRock, Inc. owned 7.6% (830,028 shares), and The Vanguard Group owned 6.6% (723,314 shares) ([Medifast DEF 14A FY2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/910329/000162828025020673/med-20250429.htm))
thesis.red_flags: Medifast reported a 34.3% year-over-year revenue decline in Q1 2026, with active earning coaches down 44.9%, showing heavy dependence on the coach network and weak client acquisition. Official risk disclosures also highlight GLP-1 competition, the challenge of maintaining and growing coaches, direct-to-consumer and supply-chain risks, product liability, regulatory exposure, and the possibility of internal control failures. ([Medifast IR](https://ir.medifastinc.com/news/news-details/2026/Medifast-Announces-First-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx), [SEC 10-Q/8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/910329/000162828026029812/med-20260504.htm))
thesis.insider_ownership: Insiders collectively own approximately US$4.4 million worth of stock (roughly 3% of the ~US$147 million company at the time reported) ([Simply Wall St - Medifast ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/household/nyse-med/medifast/ownership))

thesis.business_description: McRae Industries, Inc. operates two segments: a Military Division manufacturing combat boots for the U.S. government under multiple Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Troop Support contracts (collectively worth ~$129 million), and a Commercial Division making Western/lifestyle and work boots under the Dan Post, Laredo, Dingo, McRae Industrial and McRae Footwear brands.
thesis.competitive_position: McRae is a long-tenured (founded 1959), specialized U.S. military-boot manufacturer with multi-decade DLA contract relationships dating back to Vietnam-era jungle boots, giving it qualification/incumbency advantages in military footwear procurement, supplemented by a diversified Western/work-boot commercial business; it is a small, under-followed niche manufacturer rather than a scale player. Source: [company history via Substack](https://investingjournalbyseyi.substack.com/p/mcrae-from-kids-products-to-military-supplier).
thesis.main_shareholders: The McRae family controls the company through a dual-class structure; per the company's last detailed disclosure found (2005 filing), the family owned about 40% of Class A shares and 60% of Class B shares, together controlling approximately 53% of total votes — effective founder-family control, though this specific percentage is dated and may have changed since. The company remains majority family-owned per more recent qualitative descriptions. Source: [McRae Footwear company blog](https://mcraefootwear.com/blog/all-in-the-family).
thesis.insider_ownership: Now in its third generation of McRae family leadership (founder Branson McRae's children Gary and Jim, and grandchildren Jay and Branson Jr., hold operating/management roles), with family members collectively holding majority voting control as described above; precise current-year percentages were not found in this search. Source: [company blog](https://mcraefootwear.com/blog/all-in-the-family).
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in this search; no litigation, accounting or regulatory issues surfaced. Family dual-class control concentrates governance power, a structural item to note rather than a scandal. Source: [McRae corporate profile PDF](http://www.mcraeindustries.com/pdf/McRae_18AR.pdf).

name: George Risk Industries, Inc.

thesis.business_description: Manufacturer of electronic security and access-control devices for commercial and residential markets
thesis.competitive_position: George Risk Industries appears to be a niche manufacturer of security and alarm-related products, with an established small-cap presence built around branded hardware and low-volume specialized products rather than broad-line distribution. I could not reliably confirm its current competitor set from the accessible official filings in this session, but the company’s position is typically tied to serving specialized commercial/security customers from a narrow product line.
thesis.red_flags: The main risk appears to be concentration: a relatively narrow product portfolio and niche end markets can make results dependent on a small number of products and customer channels. I was not able to verify any recent SEC/annual-report governance or accounting issues from the accessible official filings in this session.
thesis.insider_ownership: Director Bonita Risk (Risk founding family) beneficially owned approximately 60.19% of outstanding stock (2,947,128 shares) as of April 30, 2024, including via the Kenneth Risk Trust (2,187,056 shares) and the Bonita Risk Family Irrevocable Trust (732,470 shares); historically (2015) all officers and directors as a group held 58.7% ([George Risk Industries 10-K FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/84112/000149315224029743/form10-k.htm))

industry: Industrials / Security Equipment — Manufacturer of electronic security and access-control devices for commercial and residential markets

thesis.business_description: DLH Holdings Corp. provides technology-enabled business process outsourcing, program management, public health research/analytics, healthcare IT, and systems engineering/C5ISR services to U.S. federal government agencies (including the National Institutes of Health and Defense Health Agency), covering case management, health examinations, biological research, disaster/emergency response staffing, and modeling/simulation.
thesis.competitive_position: DLH is a mid-sized federal government services contractor (~$395.9M FY2024 revenue, +5.3% YoY) with deep, multi-decade relationships with health-focused federal agencies, positioning it as a specialized niche player in federal health/IT services rather than a large-scale defense prime; its moat rests on contract incumbency and security/compliance clearances rather than technology differentiation. See [company overview](https://www.zoominfo.com/c/dlh-holdings-corp/345972107).
thesis.main_shareholders: No founder/management control; largest shareholders are activist-oriented investment firms — Wynnefield Capital, Inc. (~26%) and Mink Brook Asset Management LLC (~18.47%, which made a fresh open-market purchase of 199,099 shares on October 1, 2026) — together with the top 7 shareholders holding roughly 51% of the company, indicating concentrated but non-family institutional/activist ownership. Sources: [Yahoo Finance ownership article](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/dlh-holdings-corp-nasdaq-dlhc-191524604.html), [MarketBeat insider buying alert](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/insider-insider-buying-dlh-nasdaq-dlhc-major-shareholder-purchases-199099-shares-of-stock-2026-10-02/).
thesis.insider_ownership: Insiders hold about 14% of the company; named insiders include Zachary Parker (~3.79%) and Kathryn M. JohnBull (~3.52%). Source: [aggregator insider ownership data](https://fintel.io/so/us/dlhc).
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in this search; no litigation, accounting or governance issues surfaced. Heavy reliance on U.S. federal government contracts/budgets is an inherent sector risk (not company-specific misconduct) worth noting for a government-services business like DLH.

name: Spectra Systems Corporation

thesis.business_description: Hotel management software and cloud booking solutions for hospitality operators
thesis.competitive_position: Spectra Systems is a niche security and authentication company focused on banknote security features and related authentication technologies, serving central banks and currency printers rather than mass-market customers. Its positioning is supported by long-lived customer relationships and a specialized product set in a market dominated by a small number of security-printing and authentication suppliers.
thesis.main_shareholders: Institutional investors hold approximately 33-35% of shares in aggregate and individual/retail investors hold approximately 41-44%, per recent ownership breakdowns; the top 8 shareholders together hold more than half of the share register (specific institution names were not disclosed in the source found) ([Simply Wall St / Yahoo Finance - Spectra Systems ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/tech/aim-spsc/spectra-systems-shares/ownership))
thesis.red_flags: The company discloses a concentrated exposure to specialized government and currency-printing customers, so order timing and program wins can be lumpy. Its filings also highlight ongoing net losses and dependence on continued product adoption and government approvals for newer products.
thesis.insider_ownership: Insiders hold approximately UK£14m of stock in the ~UK£104m company (roughly 13% of the company by this estimate) ([Simply Wall St - Spectra Systems ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/tech/aim-spsc/spectra-systems-shares/ownership))

industry: Technology / Software — Hotel management software and cloud booking solutions for hospitality operators

thesis.business_description: Logistic Properties of the Americas develops, owns and manages institutional-quality industrial/logistics real estate (warehouses/distribution centers) in Costa Rica, Colombia, Peru and increasingly Mexico, leasing to multinational and regional e-commerce retailers, third-party logistics operators, and consumer-goods distributors; it became public via a 2024 SPAC merger (with TWOA, a blank-check company co-founded by an Eventbrite co-founder).
thesis.competitive_position: LPA positions itself as a leading developer/owner of institutional-grade logistics real estate in high-growth, high-barrier-to-entry Central/South American markets (18 buildings in Costa Rica, 5 in Colombia, 5 in Peru as of recent disclosure), benefiting from nearshoring trends; it reported reaching 100% occupancy across its operating portfolio in a 2025 release, though it has also been selling assets (e.g., a $152M Bogotá portfolio sale) to fund new development and delever. Sources: [BusinessWire on 100% occupancy](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250303228213/en/Logistic-Properties-of-the-Americas-Reaches-100-Occupancy-in-its-Operating-Portfolio-Across-Its-Platform), [GuruFocus on Bogotá sale](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9109529/logistic-properties-of-the-americas-lpa-sells-bogot-logistics-portfolio-for-152m).
thesis.main_shareholders: Controlled by its pre-SPAC sponsor group: Jaguar Growth Partners, LLC holds approximately 83.23% of shares (consistent with legacy 'LLP shareholders' owning ~83% post-merger), with SPAC sponsor entity HC PropTech Partners III LLC holding ~6.74% and Cerity Partners ~0.74%. This is effectively a controlled company post-SPAC. Source: [TradingKey shareholder structure](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/lpa/ownership).
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is dominated by the Jaguar Growth Partners sponsor/control group (~83%) described above rather than individual officer holdings; no additional separate management ownership data was found in this search.
thesis.red_flags: Notable financial-distress indicators: LPA has breached loan covenants previously and obtained waivers (e.g., a waiver obtained June 26, 2024), has been increasing leverage via new debt issuance over the past three years, and carries a reported Altman Z-Score of 0.61 (distress zone) with negative trailing profit margin (~-79%) and negative ROE (~-12%) per aggregator analysis; $97.7M of its debt was variable-rate as of Dec. 31, 2024, creating interest-rate sensitivity. Investors have also flagged concerns about asset quality in its Colombia portfolio. These are real balance-sheet/credit risks to weigh carefully, though no fraud or litigation was identified. Sources: [TipRanks risk factors](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lpa/risk-factors), [Cundill Deep Value report](https://cundilldeepvalue.substack.com/p/deep-value-report-logistic-properties-79c).

thesis.business_description: Canterbury Park Holding Corporation owns and operates Canterbury Park, a horse racing track, card club (poker room), and entertainment/hospitality complex in Shakopee, Minnesota, and has expanded into mixed-use real estate development around the property.
thesis.competitive_position: Canterbury Park holds a regional niche as one of the only licensed horse racing and card club venues in Minnesota, giving it a geographically protected gaming/entertainment position, supplemented by real estate development on its surrounding land. [Canterbury Park Holding FY2024 DEF 14A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1672909/000143774924013344/cphc20240425c_def14a.htm).
thesis.main_shareholders: GAMCO Investors (per Amendment 26 to Schedule 13D, filed November 15, 2023) and Black Diamond Capital Management/Stephen H. Deckhoff (per Amendment No. 5 to Schedule 13G, filed February 14, 2024) are both disclosed as >5% holders. [Canterbury Park Holding FY2024 DEF 14A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1672909/000143774924013344/cphc20240425c_def14a.htm).
thesis.insider_ownership: President/CEO Randall (Randy) Sampson is the largest individual-linked holder: per a Schedule 13G/A as of December 31, 2025, he beneficially owned 997,013 shares, comprising 261,923 held directly, 33,530 held jointly with his spouse, 34,173 in a family trust (as sole trustee, disclaimed), and 667,387 held through Sampson Family Real Estate Holdings, LLC (as sole manager, disclaimed). [Canterbury Park Schedule 13G/A FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001672909/000167290926000005/primary_doc.xml). Aggregator data (undated) puts total individual insider ownership at roughly 23.2%, with top 25 shareholders owning ~76%. [Canterbury Park ownership - SimplyWall.st](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/consumer-services/nasdaq-cphc/canterbury-park-holding/ownership).
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in this search.

thesis.business_description: Duluth Holdings Inc. (Duluth Trading Company) is a Belleville, Wisconsin-based designer, marketer, and retailer of men's and women's casual and workwear apparel, footwear, and accessories, sold through e-commerce, catalog, and company-operated retail stores.
thesis.competitive_position: Duluth Trading is a niche workwear/outdoor-lifestyle apparel brand known for durable, function-first clothing (e.g., "Buck Naked" underwear, Fire Hose fabric pants) with a multichannel (direct and store-based) model; it competes against larger apparel and workwear retailers and has faced recent retail-sector margin pressure. [Duluth Holdings ownership - SimplyWall.st](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/retail/nasdaq-dlth/duluth-holdings/ownership).
thesis.main_shareholders: Founder Stephen L. Schlecht is the largest shareholder, reporting 3,364,200 Class A shares (held via the Duluth Holdings Inc. Voting Trust, of which he is sole trustee) and 7,119,588 Class B shares as of a 2026 Schedule 13G/A -- roughly 28.6% of total shares per aggregator calculation. The Stephen L. Schlecht and Marianne M. Schlecht Descendants Trust separately holds approximately 23.7% (8,694,295 Class B shares per aggregator data). [Duluth Holdings Schedule 13G/A FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649744/000089271226000098/primary_doc.xml); [Duluth Holdings ownership - SimplyWall.st](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/retail/nasdaq-dlth/duluth-holdings/ownership).
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder-family insider ownership is very high: Stephen Schlecht (~28.6%) plus the Schlecht Descendants Trust (~23.7%) together account for roughly half the company; individual insiders in aggregate are estimated at ~42.4% per SimplyWall.st. Relative Richard Schlecht (SVP) holds a smaller stake (~1.2%, ~441,893 shares) and bought 28,554 shares on Dec 24, 2025. Stephen Schlecht gifted 102,000 Class B shares between the FY2025 and FY2026 13G/A filings. [Duluth Holdings Schedule 13G/A FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649744/000089271226000098/primary_doc.xml); [Duluth Holdings ownership - SimplyWall.st](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/retail/nasdaq-dlth/duluth-holdings/ownership).
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in this search; the dual-class structure (Class A held via a voting trust controlled by the founder) concentrates voting control with the Schlecht family, limiting influence of Class B public shareholders, a structural feature rather than a disclosed impropriety.

thesis.business_description: Northern Technologies International Corporation develops and markets proprietary corrosion-prevention products and services under the ZERUST brand, and bio-based/biodegradable plastics under the Natur-Tec brand, sold in over 65 countries directly and through subsidiaries, joint ventures, and distributors.
thesis.competitive_position: NTIC holds a specialized niche as a long-established (50+ year) global leader in corrosion-prevention packaging and coatings for automotive, industrial, mining, and oil & gas customers, supplemented by a smaller bioplastics business; its moat is proprietary ZERUST formulations and an entrenched global distributor/JV network rather than scale. [Company overview](https://money.usnews.com/investing/stocks/ntic-northern-technologies-international-corp)
thesis.main_shareholders: Largest disclosed holders include Inter Alia Holding Company (~13%), Needham Investment Management L.L.C. (~7.51%), Vanguard Capital Management LLC (~4.04%), and Dimensional Fund Advisors L.P. (~3.51%). [TradingKey ownership data](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/ntic/ownership)
thesis.insider_ownership: Insiders collectively hold approximately 4.86% of shares across roughly 9 reporting holders (~$3.43 million in value); CEO G. Patrick Lynch directly holds about 1.1% of shares outstanding. [TradingKey ownership data](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/ntic/ownership)
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.

name: AMCON Distributing Company

thesis.business_description: Wholesale distributor of tobacco, candy, beverages, groceries, and other convenience-store products
thesis.competitive_position: AMCON Distributing Company is a niche wholesale distributor with a broadline mix centered on cigarettes and tobacco products, plus candy, beverages, foodservice, groceries, and HBC goods; it also operates health food retail stores in the Midwest and Florida. Its public website describes it as headquartered in Omaha and organized around wholesale distribution plus specialty retail, which differentiates it from pure-play food distributors and from tobacco-only wholesalers ([AMCON Distributing Company](https://www.amcon.com)).
thesis.red_flags: The company’s disclosed business mix is highly exposed to tobacco and cigarettes, a category facing long-term volume decline and regulatory pressure. The public website also indicates a secondary health-food retail segment, which adds operational complexity and a smaller, less scalable business line ([AMCON Distributing Company](https://www.amcon.com)).

industry: Consumer Discretionary / Food Distribution — Wholesale distributor of tobacco, candy, beverages, groceries, and other convenience-store products

thesis.business_description: Nuvera Communications, Inc. (formerly New Ulm Telecom, Inc., marketing name adopted 2018) is a Minnesota-based holding company whose wholly-owned subsidiaries (Hutchinson Telephone, Peoples Telephone, Scott-Rice Telephone, Sleepy Eye Telephone, Western Telephone) provide rural telephone, broadband, and related telecom services, plus minority equity interests in several regional fiber/broadband joint ventures.
thesis.competitive_position: Nuvera is a small, diversified rural incumbent local exchange carrier (ILEC) group dating to 1905, with minority stakes (ranging 7.5%-24.3%) in regional fiber ventures (FiberComm, Broadband Visions, Independent Emergency Services, Fiber Minnesota) that provide additional diversification beyond its core wireline telecom base. [Nuvera Communications FY2022 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/71557/000151316223000040/nuvr-20221231.htm).
thesis.main_shareholders: Minerva Advisors LLC is reported as the largest single holder at roughly 19.4% per SimplyWall.st aggregator data (undated, likely circa 2025); top 16 shareholders reportedly own about 33% of the company. [Nuvera Communications ownership - SimplyWall.st](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/telecom/otc-nuvr/nuvera-communications/ownership).
thesis.insider_ownership: Aggregator estimates of insider ownership conflict: SimplyWall.st shows individual insiders at ~11.2% (institutions ~21.8%, public ~67%), while MarketBeat shows insiders at ~13.8% and institutions at ~13.35%. For current figures, consult the company's latest 10-K security-ownership section or proxy statement. [Nuvera Communications ownership - SimplyWall.st](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/telecom/otc-nuvr/nuvera-communications/ownership).
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in this search.

name: Flexible Solutions International, Inc.

thesis.business_description: Specialty biodegradable polymers and water-treatment products for agriculture, oil & gas, and cleaning markets
thesis.competitive_position: Flexible Solutions International is a small-cap specialty chemicals company that says it operates through Flexible Solutions Ltd., NanoChem Solutions, and ENP LLC, with products and operations centered on water-loss control, water treatment, and related chemical solutions. Its niche appears to be specialty, lower-volume formulations rather than commoditized bulk chemicals, but public materials do not disclose market share; the most direct competitive framing available from the company is its product-and-segment presentation on the investor page and its ongoing product-development announcements. [Flexible Solutions investor info](https://flexiblesolutions.com/investor-info/)
thesis.main_shareholders: Founder/insider Daniel B. O'Brien held approximately 37.0% of shares (4,521,900 shares) as of Jan 16, 2020, up from 34.3% in 2014; Dr. Robert N. O'Brien held approximately 13.7% (1,805,000 shares) as of 2014 ([Flexible Solutions International DEF 14A FY2020](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1069394/000100487820000012/definproxyfeb1-20.txt))
thesis.red_flags: The investor page shows a very small equity base, with 12,680,532 shares outstanding as of September 30, 2025, which can amplify liquidity and governance risk. [Flexible Solutions investor info](https://flexiblesolutions.com/investor-info/)
thesis.insider_ownership: The O'Brien family are the controlling insiders: Daniel B. O'Brien held approximately 37.0% of shares as of Jan 16, 2020 ([Flexible Solutions International DEF 14A FY2020](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1069394/000100487820000012/definproxyfeb1-20.txt))

industry: Materials / Specialty Chemicals — Specialty biodegradable polymers and water-treatment products for agriculture, oil & gas, and cleaning markets

name: Sono-Tek Corporation

thesis.business_description: Designs and manufactures ultrasonic coating systems for medical, semiconductor, industrial, and energy applications
thesis.competitive_position: Sono-Tek describes itself as the global leader in ultrasonic coating systems for precision thin film deposition, serving medical, semiconductor, energy, and industrial manufacturing customers ([Sono-Tek](https://sonotek.com)). Its niche is a specialized process-control platform for high-uniformity coatings rather than broad industrial equipment, which places it against fewer direct peers than general coating or deposition vendors ([Sono-Tek](https://sonotek.com)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Emancipation Management LLC held 34.7% of common stock (5,472,052 shares) as of December 31, 2024 ([Sono-Tek SC 13G/A FY2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000806172/000108514625000021/primary_doc.xml))
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.
thesis.insider_ownership: Per an older proxy filing, all executive officers and directors as a group owned approximately 22.7% of shares; other historical 5%+ owners included Norwood Venture Corporation (18.6%) and Herbert Spiegel (5.6%) (dates not confirmed as current) ([Sono-Tek DEF 14A filings - SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/806172/000117152022000416/eps10354.htm))

industry: Industrials / Industrial Machinery — Designs and manufactures ultrasonic coating systems for medical, semiconductor, industrial, and energy applications

thesis.business_description: Bridgford Foods Corporation manufactures and distributes frozen food products (biscuits, bread/roll dough items) and snack food products (dry sausage, beef jerky, ready-to-eat sandwiches, non-refrigerated snacks), operating through Frozen Food Products and Snack Food Products segments.
thesis.competitive_position: Bridgford is a long-established (founded 1932), family-controlled food manufacturer that pioneered the frozen dough category and has more recently seen growth from its shelf-stable snack/jerky segment; with ~$228.2M revenue it is a small-cap niche player competing against much larger packaged-food companies, relying on long-standing retail relationships and category heritage rather than brand dominance. Source: [company profile](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/brid/company/).
thesis.main_shareholders: The Bridgford family controls the company overwhelmingly: Bridgford Industries Incorporated holds approximately 78.84% of shares (7,156,396 shares as of June 2, 2026), with the family's aggregate beneficial ownership cited at approximately 80% of outstanding stock. Source: [WallStreetZen/aggregator ownership data](https://uk.investing.com/equities/bridgford-foods-c-ownership).
thesis.insider_ownership: Extremely high founder-family insider control (~80% aggregate), with over 60 family members across five generations historically involved in the business and currently two Bridgford family members on the Board of Directors and two on the Executive Committee — a classic closely-held family-controlled public company. Source: [company history](https://www.bridgfordfoods.com/why-bridgford/our-history/).
thesis.red_flags: No material legal proceedings were pending as of October 31, 2025 per the company's most recent filing. A historical material weakness in internal control over financial reporting was identified in the FY2022 10-K (failure to timely report a change in lease terms from month-to-month to a five-year term), since remediated. The company also changed auditors in April 2026 (dismissing Baker Tilly US, LLP and appointing Withum Smith+Brown, PC), though Baker Tilly's prior opinions contained no adverse/disclaimed findings and the company reported no disagreements — a routine auditor transition, not an adverse signal. Sources: [SEC 10-K FY2023](https://www.bridgford.com/corporate/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/Form-10K-FY23.pdf), [auditor-change coverage](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/BRID/8-k.html).

thesis.main_shareholders: As of April 10, 2023: Dimensional Fund Advisors LP held 7.4% (547,916 shares) and Royce & Associates, LP held 7.0% (518,570 shares) ([AstroNova DEF 14A FY2023](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/8146/000119312523122091/d345299ddef14a.htm))
thesis.insider_ownership: The Board of Directors and executive officers collectively beneficially own approximately 16.6% of common stock per the most recent proxy; insider Peter Kamin made a notable recent purchase of ~US*k of shares ([AstroNova insider ownership tracking / DEF 14A filings](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/astronova-insider-ups-holding-during-131643389.html))
thesis.business_description: AstroNova, Inc. is a global provider of specialty printing technologies, operating through a Product Identification segment (digital label/packaging printers, hardware, software, and supplies) and an Aerospace segment (flight-deck printers, avionics networking hardware, and aerospace-grade supplies).
thesis.competitive_position: AstroNova describes itself as a market leader in tabletop digital color label printing and in flight-deck/cockpit printers, and an innovator in digital color mini-press systems, maintaining its position through proprietary technology, product reputation, and established distribution/service channels; management has stated a strategy to reaccelerate revenue growth while defending its leadership in cockpit printers. [AstroNova press release on label press launch](https://www.astronovainc.com/astronova-sends-letter-to-shareholders-highlighting-growth-strategy-and-strength-of-board/)
thesis.red_flags: AstroNova and its Portuguese subsidiary (AstroNova Portugal) faced arbitration proceedings initiated in March 2025 by Effort Premier Solutions LDA and an individual (Elói Serafim Alves Ferreira) alleging breaches of the MTEX acquisition agreement and reputational damage; the matter was resolved via settlement agreement in May 2026. [AstroNova 10-Q disclosure](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/8146/000119312525314060/alot-20251031.htm)

name: Supremex Inc.

thesis.business_description: Manufacturer of envelopes and paper-based packaging solutions for North American commercial customers
thesis.competitive_position: Supremex is a Canadian envelope and paper-based packaging specialist with a North American footprint, serving large national/multinational customers, direct mailers, and e-commerce packaging users. Its niche is a combination of envelope manufacturing scale and a diversified packaging line, competing in envelopes against other North American suppliers and in packaging against specialized folding-carton and e-commerce packaging firms.
thesis.main_shareholders: George Christopoulos is the largest named shareholder of Supremex Inc. with approximately 11.4% of shares outstanding (2,781,696 shares); other named holders include Stewart Emerson (about 0.86%) and Robert Johnston (about 0.61%) ([Supremex Inc. ownership, GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/TSX:SXP/ownership)).
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.
thesis.insider_ownership: Individual insiders hold approximately 13.1% of Supremex Inc. in aggregate, led by George Christopoulos's approximately 11.4% stake ([Supremex Inc. ownership, GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/TSX:SXP/ownership)).

industry: Materials / Packaging — Manufacturer of envelopes and paper-based packaging solutions for North American commercial customers

name: Flanigan's Enterprises, Inc.

thesis.business_description: Operates full-service casual dining restaurants and bars in South Florida
thesis.competitive_position: Flanigan's Enterprises operates a South Florida restaurant chain centered on its Flanigan's Seafood Bar and Grill concept, giving it a localized, family-run niche rather than a national scale position ([Flanigan's website](https://www.flanigans.net), [SEC filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/12040/000207709626000171/0002077096-26-000171-index.htm)). Its competitive set is primarily other casual-dining and sports-bar operators in Florida, but the company’s filings available here did not disclose formal market share figures or a ranked position versus named peers ([SEC filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/12040/000207709626000171/0002077096-26-000171-index.htm)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Not disclosed in public filings
thesis.red_flags: The public filing reviewed here was a Form 4, so it does not provide operating risks or a shareholder base; broader risks must be taken from the company’s 10-K/proxy, which were not located in the available SEC search results ([SEC filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/12040/000207709626000171/0002077096-26-000171-index.htm)). No material red flags were identified from the official sources reviewed, but the research set was limited to the company website and the Form 4 index page ([Flanigan's website](https://www.flanigans.net), [SEC filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/12040/000207709626000171/0002077096-26-000171-index.htm)).

industry: Consumer Discretionary / Restaurants — Operates full-service casual dining restaurants and bars in South Florida

thesis.main_shareholders: PenderFund Capital Management Ltd. holds approximately 13.4% of Sylogist Ltd., Seymour Investment Management Ltd. holds about 10.9%, and EdgePoint Investment Group Inc. holds about 10.8% ([Sylogist Ltd. ownership, GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/SYZLF/ownership)).
thesis.insider_ownership: Individual insiders hold approximately 3.62% of Sylogist Ltd. (about CA$13 million worth of shares) ([Sylogist Ltd. ownership, GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/SYZLF/ownership)).
thesis.business_description: Sylogist Ltd. is a SaaS software company providing ERP, CRM, fundraising, education-administration, and payments solutions to K-12/higher-education institutions, plus fund accounting, grant management, and payroll software to government and nonprofit public-sector organizations, across the U.S., Canada, the U.K., and other regions.
thesis.competitive_position: Sylogist serves over 2,000 government, nonprofit, and education organizations with a Microsoft-aligned platform and a disciplined acquisition strategy, positioning itself not as a broad enterprise-software vendor but as a provider of narrow, hard-to-replace, compliance-driven software with high customer retention in markets where switching is costly due to specialized regulatory workflows. [Bitget company overview](https://www.bitget.com/stock/tsx-syz/what-is)
thesis.red_flags: Sylogist is in the midst of an active, contentious proxy fight: activist investor OneMove Capital Ltd. (led by Tyler Proud) requisitioned a Special Shareholder Meeting (held/scheduled April 7, 2026) seeking to take four of seven board seats despite holding a much smaller ownership stake; Sylogist says shareholders holding over 35% of the company (including largest holder PenderFund Capital Management) oppose the requisition, and that the board's settlement offers were rebuffed by OneMove. This represents a live governance/board-control dispute. [Bloomberg on activist dispute](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-07/activist-investor-onemove-says-sylogist-board-blocked-settlement-talks) / [TipRanks on special meeting](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/sylogist-adds-independent-director-and-resets-shareholder-meeting-amid-activist-dispute)

thesis.business_description: Air T, Inc. is a Charlotte, North Carolina-based diversified holding company operating in overnight air cargo (Mountain Air Cargo and CSA Air, flying feeder routes for FedEx Express under long-term dry-lease contracts with roughly 103-105 aircraft), ground support equipment manufacturing (Global Ground Support -- deicers, lifts, decontamination units, tow tractors), commercial aircraft/engine/parts trading and leasing (Air T Global Leasing, formed 2015), and digital aviation solutions.

thesis.main_shareholders: The founding Gordon family controls roughly 23% (one source) up to a higher aggregate depending on methodology; named family holders include CEO/CFO Andrew Gordon (~10.9%, 661,750 shares), COO David Gordon (~10.9%, 655,037 shares), and Rachelle L. Gordon and founder Sterling A. Gordon (~9.53% each, 544,082 shares each) — i.e., a classic founder-family-controlled microcap. Source: [TipRanks ownership data](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/jva/ownership).
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is effectively the Gordon family block described above; CEO Andrew Gordon and COO David Gordon have each been with the company 30+ years, indicating long-tenured, hands-on family management control. thesis.red_flags: Notable current red flag: Coffee Holding has disclosed UNREMEDIATED material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting spanning fiscal years 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023 (as of the most recent disclosure found), a multi-year, still-open control deficiency that warrants real caution on financial-statement reliability. Separately, a proposed 2022 merger/share-exchange with Delta Corp Holdings Limited (which would have redomiciled the combined company to the Cayman Islands) was terminated in June 2024 after failing to win shareholder approval in a March 2024 vote (no termination fee was incurred); an M&A-related shareholder litigation-investigation firm had examined that now-abandoned deal. The company also sued a logistics broker in January 2025 over a missing ~$84,500 coffee shipment (routine commercial litigation, not a governance concern). Current (FY2024) 10-K reports no other material legal proceedings. Sources: [TipRanks risk factors](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/jva/risk-factors), [TipRanks on merger termination](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/coffee-holding-co-ends-merger-deal-with-delta-corp).
